check_action: Check ABS fuse and harness connector pins for corrosion or bent terminals.
safety_warning: ABS failure may cause wheels to lock up during emergency braking. Drive with caution.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check ABS fuse
diagnosis_steps.title: Check the ABS Fuse in the Engine Bay Box
diagnosis_steps.description: Locate the ABS / ESP fuse in the fuse diagram and pull it with plastic tweezers to check the internal metal link.

results.label: Blown fuse
results.explanation: A blown fuse cuts power to the ABS solenoid block and computer module.
results.recommended_action: Replace with identical amperage fuse. If it blows again immediately, a short circuit exists.

results.label: Intact fuse
results.explanation: Fuse has electrical continuity. Power delivery upstream is likely functional.
results.recommended_action: Proceed to harness wiring and sensor tests.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect wiring to ABS module
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Wiring Harness and Connector to ABS Module
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine the multi-pin connector on the hydraulic control unit for loose pins, water ingress or chafed cables.

results.label: Faulty wiring / corroded pins
results.explanation: Damaged wiring prevents communication between the wheel sensors, ECU, and ABS pump.
results.recommended_action: Clean pins with electrical contact cleaner or repair damaged harness wires.

results.label: Good wiring & secure connector
results.explanation: Wiring and physical connectivity are sound. Internal electronic or solenoid failure suspected.
results.recommended_action: Perform an OBD2 scan to read specific ABS fault codes (e.g., C0035, C0040).

repair_guide.title: ABS Control Module Inspection & Connector Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Turn ignition completely OFF before disconnecting the ABS module connector.

steps.title: Turn Off Vehicle & Disconnect Battery
steps.description: Ensure vehicle is parked safely on level ground. Turn off ignition and remove key.

steps.title: Inspect ABS Main Fuses
steps.description: Check both the 30A/40A pump motor fuse and the 10A module logic fuse in the fuse box.

steps.title: Unclip and Clean Module Harness
steps.description: Release the locking latch on the ABS block, check for green oxidation, spray contact cleaner and re-seat firmly.

check_action: Inspect wheel hub area for broken sensor cable or magnetic ring debris.
safety_warning: Avoid sudden aggressive maneuvers on wet surfaces while the ABS light remains active.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect wheel speed sensor connections
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Wheel Speed Sensor Connectors in Wheel Wells
diagnosis_steps.description: Check the electrical connector behind the wheel liner for loose locking clips or severed wires from road debris.

results.label: Loose / damaged connections
results.explanation: A severed or intermittent wire interrupts the wheel rotation frequency signal.
results.recommended_action: Re-clip or splice the sensor harness.

results.label: Secure & intact connections
results.explanation: Electrical harness continuity looks normal up to the knuckle.
results.recommended_action: Inspect the magnetic sensor head and reluctor ring.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check wheel speed sensor for debris or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Sensor Tip & Reluctor Ring for Metal Debris or Cracks
diagnosis_steps.description: Look at the magnetic pickup tip and the toothed tone ring on the wheel hub or CV joint.

results.label: Dirty / metallic debris / cracked ring
results.explanation: Metallic brake dust or a cracked tone ring distorts the pulse signal sent to the ABS computer.
results.recommended_action: Clean the sensor head with brake cleaner or replace the cracked reluctor ring.

results.label: Clean and intact
results.explanation: Physical condition is clean. Internal coil resistance may have failed.
results.recommended_action: Measure internal resistance with a multimeter (standard 800 - 1500 ohms).

repair_guide.title: Wheel Speed Sensor Cleaning & Resistance Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never work under a vehicle supported only by a hydraulic jack. Always use jack stands.

steps.title: Raise Wheel & Remove Tire
steps.description: Loosen lug nuts, raise vehicle corner, secure on jack stand and remove wheel.

steps.title: Unbolt Sensor from Knuckle
steps.description: Remove single 10mm bolt holding sensor to steering knuckle. Gently twist and pull sensor out.

steps.title: Clean Sensor Tip & Tone Ring
steps.description: Wipe metal filings and grease off sensor tip. Rotate hub and spray tone ring with brake cleaner.

symptoms: Hissing noise under dashboard when braking
check_action: Test vacuum hose between intake manifold and booster for cracks or air leaks.
safety_warning: A failing brake booster dramatically increases stopping distance. Do not drive on public roads.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check brake booster vacuum hose
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Brake Booster Vacuum Hose and One-Way Check Valve
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect the thick rubber vacuum hose connecting the engine intake manifold or vacuum pump to the brake booster.

results.label: Leaking / split / disconnected hose
results.explanation: Vacuum loss prevents the booster diaphragm from multiplying pedal effort, making the pedal rock hard.
results.recommended_action: Replace the cracked vacuum hose and check the one-way valve.

results.label: Intact hose with firm vacuum
results.explanation: Vacuum supply is present. Internal diaphragm leak or master cylinder seal issue suspected.
results.recommended_action: Perform static pedal holding test.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test brake booster vacuum pressure
diagnosis_steps.title: Pump Brake Pedal with Engine Off then Start Engine
diagnosis_steps.description: Pump the brake pedal 5 times with engine off until firm, hold pedal down, and start the engine.

results.label: Pedal stays hard, does not drop slightly
results.explanation: Internal booster diaphragm ruptured or vacuum pump failure.
results.recommended_action: Replace the brake booster assembly.

results.label: Pedal drops smoothly about 1-2 cm
results.explanation: Booster vacuum assist is functioning properly.
results.recommended_action: If pedal is still spongy, inspect for air in hydraulic lines or caliper leaks.

repair_guide.title: Brake Booster Vacuum Functional Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Perform test while safely parked with handbrake firmly engaged.

steps.title: Deplete Residual Vacuum
steps.description: With engine off, pump brake pedal firmly 5 to 6 times until pedal travel becomes noticeably short and hard.

steps.title: Hold Pressure & Start Engine
steps.description: Keep medium foot pressure on pedal and turn ignition on to idle. The pedal should sink slightly.

symptoms: Burning smell or very hot wheel hub
check_action: Inspect caliper for brake fluid weeping around piston seal or seized guide slide pins.
safety_warning: A seized dragging caliper causes extreme brake overheating, rotor warping, and fluid boil vapor lock.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect brake caliper for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Brake Caliper Body and Piston Dust Boot for Fluid
diagnosis_steps.description: Look through wheel spokes or behind wheel for wet oily residue around the caliper piston boot and bleed screw.

results.label: Leaking brake fluid
results.explanation: Piston seal failure leaks hydraulic fluid, causing sudden pedal sponginess and total brake failure.
results.recommended_action: Rebuild caliper with fresh seal kit or replace caliper immediately.

results.label: No fluid leaks detected
results.explanation: Hydraulic sealing is intact.
results.recommended_action: Check mechanical slide pins and piston return motion.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check brake caliper piston operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Piston & Guide Slide Pin Freedom of Movement
diagnosis_steps.description: Jack up wheel and rotate by hand, apply brake pedal, release and check if wheel spins freely again.

results.label: Stuck piston / wheel locked or hard to rotate
results.explanation: Corroded caliper piston or seized slide pins keep the brake pad clamped against the rotor.
results.recommended_action: Remove caliper, lubricate slide pins with silicone brake grease or replace caliper.

results.label: Free-moving piston / wheel rotates freely after release
results.explanation: Caliper mechanical release is operating normally.
results.recommended_action: Inspect brake pad wear taper and rotor surface.

repair_guide.title: Brake Caliper Slide Pin Lubrication & Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not allow the caliper to hang by the rubber brake hose. Support it with a wire hook.

steps.title: Lift Vehicle and Remove Wheel
steps.description: Secure vehicle, remove wheel and locate caliper mounting bolts.

steps.title: Remove and Inspect Guide Pins
steps.description: Unscrew slide pin bolts, pull pins out of rubber boots, clean old gummy grease with cloth.

steps.title: Apply Synthetic Brake Grease
steps.description: Coat slide pins with silicone ceramic grease and ensure rubber boots seal tightly.

symptoms: Pedal sinking slowly to the floor
check_action: Visually inspect rubber hoses for cracks, bulges (aneurysms) while an assistant presses the pedal.
safety_warning: A ruptured brake hose results in immediate loss of primary hydraulic braking.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect brake hose for cracks or leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Visual & Flex Inspection of Rubber Brake Hoses
diagnosis_steps.description: Turn steering wheel to full lock and bend rubber hose gently to inspect for deep dry-rot cracking or damp spots.

results.label: Cracked, bulging or leaking hose
results.explanation: Aging rubber degrades from UV, ozone, and pressure cycles, risking sudden blowout.
results.recommended_action: Replace both left and right front/rear flexible brake hoses.

results.label: Intact hose with smooth rubber
results.explanation: Exterior rubber sheath is healthy.
results.recommended_action: Check internal hose collapse or master cylinder leak.

diagnosis_steps.step: Pressure test brake hose
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Hose Expansion Under Heavy Pedal Pressure
diagnosis_steps.description: Have a helper press the brake pedal hard while you observe the flexible hose.

results.label: Hose expands or balloons under pressure
results.explanation: Internal reinforcement braids have severed, absorbing pressure and softening the pedal feel.
results.recommended_action: Replace the flexible brake line immediately.

results.label: Passes pressure test, no swelling
results.explanation: Hose withstands full hydraulic working pressure.
results.recommended_action: Inspect brake master cylinder and caliper seals.

repair_guide.title: Brake Flexible Line Replacement & System Bleeding
repair_guide.safety_warning: Brake fluid damages car paint. Always bleed air completely from lines before driving.

steps.title: Spray Penetrating Oil on Flare Fittings
steps.description: Soak hard line metal fittings with penetrating oil 15 minutes prior to unscrewing.

steps.title: Uncouple Hose and Catch Fluid
steps.description: Use a flare nut wrench to prevent rounding the hexagonal fitting.

steps.title: Install New Hose & Bleed Brake Caliper
steps.description: Tighten banjos with new copper crush washers and bleed air bubbles until fluid runs crystal clear.

symptoms: Pedal slowly sinks to floor at red lights
check_action: Check reservoir fluid level and inspect rear of master cylinder where it bolts to booster.
safety_warning: An internal piston cup bypass causes sudden complete loss of brake pressure while stopped.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check brake fluid level in master cylinder
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Brake Fluid Reservoir Level & Color
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine clear reservoir on driver side firewall. Level should be between MIN and MAX.

results.label: Low fluid level / dark black contaminated fluid
results.explanation: Low fluid indicates either worn brake friction material or an active external hydraulic leak.
results.recommended_action: Top up with correct DOT specification fluid and inspect calipers and drums for leaks.

results.label: Normal fluid level
results.explanation: Fluid capacity is adequate.
results.recommended_action: Proceed to test internal piston seal bypass.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect master cylinder for leaks or internal bypass
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Rear Seal and Hold Constant Pedal Force
diagnosis_steps.description: Check between master cylinder flange and booster for fluid drops, and hold steady medium pressure on pedal for 30s.

results.label: Leaking at rear seal or pedal slowly creeps downward
results.explanation: Internal rubber piston cups are worn, allowing fluid to bypass between primary and secondary chambers.
results.recommended_action: Replace the brake master cylinder assembly and bench-bleed before installation.

results.label: Intact, dry and pedal holds rock steady
results.explanation: Master cylinder hydraulic integrity confirmed.
results.recommended_action: If pedal is spongy, air bubbles in caliper lines are the most probable cause.

repair_guide.title: Master Cylinder Creep Test & Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never use contaminated or opened brake fluid bottles that have absorbed ambient moisture.

steps.title: Static Hold Test
steps.description: Engine idling, press brake pedal with moderate pressure. If pedal continues slowly sinking without external leaks, master cylinder seals are bypassing.

steps.title: Examine Booster Mounting Flange
steps.description: Look under the reservoir neck and at the booster seam for peeling black paint or wet brake fluid residue.

check_action: Check friction material thickness through wheel rim opening (minimum legal 2mm - 3mm).
safety_warning: Worn out pads grinding metal-on-metal severely damage brake rotors and double braking distance.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check brake pad thickness
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Remaining Brake Pad Friction Lining
diagnosis_steps.description: Use a pad thickness gauge or flashlight through wheel rim to inspect inner and outer friction material.

results.label: Worn pads (below 3mm or backing plate touching)
results.explanation: Acoustic wear indicators or metal backing plate rubbing on rotor disc, creating high pitched squeal or grinding.
results.recommended_action: Replace front or rear brake pad axle set immediately.

results.label: Sufficient thickness (above 5mm)
results.explanation: Friction lining has substantial remaining life.
results.recommended_action: Inspect for glazed pad surface or warped brake rotor.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect brake pad condition
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect for Glazing, Cracking, or Uneven Taper Wear
diagnosis_steps.description: Check if outer pad is thick but inner pad is completely worn out (indicates sticking caliper slide pins).

results.label: Uneven / glazed / cracked pads
results.explanation: Sticking caliper guide pins cause one pad to drag continuously, overheating and glazing the friction layer.
results.recommended_action: Replace brake pads and clean/grease caliper slide pins.

results.label: Good condition pads with flat uniform wear
results.explanation: Pads are functioning properly. Squeal may be due to missing anti-squeal shims or harmless brake dust.
results.recommended_action: Clean with brake dust cleaner spray.

repair_guide.title: Brake Pad Replacement & Rotor Bedding
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not inhale brake dust. Always replace brake pads as a complete axle set (left + right).

steps.title: Disassemble Caliper Anchor
steps.description: Remove lower caliper slide pin bolt and swing caliper upward.

steps.title: Extract Old Pads & Clean Bracket
steps.description: Remove worn pads, replace stainless steel abutment clips, and wire brush bracket slots.

steps.title: Retract Piston & Install New Pads
steps.description: Push piston back into bore using retraction tool (watch reservoir fluid level), insert new pads and torque bolts to factory spec.

symptoms: Deep scoring grooves on disc surface
check_action: Run fingernail across rotor surface to detect ridges, or measure thickness variation with micrometer.
safety_warning: Severely thinned or heat-cracked rotors can shatter under panic braking.

diagnosis_steps.step: Measure brake rotor thickness
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Rotor Thickness Against Minimum Discard Spec
diagnosis_steps.description: Use a digital vernier caliper or micrometer at multiple points around the brake disc contact band.

results.label: Thin rotor below minimum thickness spec (MIN TH)
results.explanation: Rotor has lost thermal mass, overheating rapidly and risking structural fracture.
results.recommended_action: Replace brake rotors in axle pairs.

results.label: Sufficient thickness rotor
results.explanation: Rotor thickness is within allowable service limits.
results.recommended_action: Inspect rotor lateral runout and face warping.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect brake rotor for scoring or warping
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Rotor Face for Deep Grooves, Rust Lip, or Warping
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine both inner and outer friction faces for bluing (overheating), deep circular grooves, or lateral runout vibration.

results.label: Scored / warped / heat spotted rotor
results.explanation: Disc thickness variation (DTV) or lateral runout pushes the pads back, creating pulsation felt in the pedal and steering wheel.
results.recommended_action: Replace rotors along with a fresh set of matched brake pads.

results.label: Smooth and flat rotor surface
results.explanation: Rotor surface finish is within tolerance.
results.recommended_action: Check wheel bearing hub runout or loose suspension bushings.

repair_guide.title: Brake Disc Inspection & Runout Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always replace rotors in axle pairs (both fronts or both rears) to maintain symmetric braking.

steps.title: Clean Hub Face
steps.description: Remove rust from wheel hub mating flange with a wire wheel before mounting new discs.

steps.title: Mount Rotor & Check Runout
steps.description: Tighten rotor with lug nuts and check lateral runout with dial indicator (maximum allowable ~0.05mm).

symptoms: Weak parking brake hold on incline
check_action: Remove rear drum to inspect shoe friction lining and wheel cylinder dust boots for fluid seepage.
safety_warning: Contaminated brake shoes saturated with brake fluid or axle grease must never be reused.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect brake shoes for wear
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Brake Shoe Friction Material Thickness
diagnosis_steps.description: Measure curved friction lining thickness on leading and trailing shoes inside the rear drum assembly.

results.label: Worn shoes (under 1.5mm) or contaminated with fluid
results.explanation: Brake shoes worn to rivets or soaked from a leaking wheel cylinder.
results.recommended_action: Install a rear drum brake shoe kit and replace wheel cylinders.

results.label: Good condition shoes with ample lining
results.explanation: Shoe linings have good remaining thickness.
results.recommended_action: Inspect internal drum surface diameter.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check brake drum for scoring or cracks
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Cast Iron Drum Surface for Scoring, Cracks or Out-of-Round
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect the inside braking surface of the drum for deep ridges, heat bluing, or oval out-of-round shape.

results.label: Scored / cracked / oval drum
results.explanation: Warped drum causes surging braking and grabby rear wheels.
results.recommended_action: Machine or replace rear brake drums.

results.label: Smooth and uniform drum surface
results.explanation: Drum braking diameter is within tolerance.
results.recommended_action: Adjust the self-adjuster star wheel mechanism.

repair_guide.title: Rear Brake Drum Cleaning & Self-Adjuster Service
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not use compressed air to blow brake dust from drums. Use liquid brake cleaner.

steps.title: Release Handbrake and Pull Drum
steps.description: Ensure handbrake is completely down, back off adjuster star wheel through backing plate hole if drum is stuck on wear ridge.

steps.title: Inspect Wheel Cylinder Boots
steps.description: Peel back rubber boots on wheel cylinder; if brake fluid emerges, cylinder seals have failed.

symptoms: Loud noise when AC is on
check_action: Observe compressor clutch hub with AC switched ON to see if magnetic clutch engages and spins.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check AC compressor clutch operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Observe Compressor Clutch Hub Engagement
diagnosis_steps.description: Start engine, turn AC to MAX COLD. Watch the center hub plate of the AC compressor pulley.

results.label: Clutch not engaging (pulley spins but center hub stationary)
results.explanation: Low refrigerant pressure switch cutoff, blown AC clutch fuse, or open electromagnetic coil.
results.recommended_action: Check AC pressure with manifold gauge and verify 12V power at compressor connector.

results.label: Clutch engages properly (center hub spins with pulley)
results.explanation: Compressor mechanical drive is engaging.
results.recommended_action: If air is still warm, check internal compressor displacement valves or condenser airflow.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect AC compressor for leaks or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Compressor Body for Green UV Dye or Black Sludge
diagnosis_steps.description: Look around the front shaft seal and case halves for oily green residue or metal shavings.

results.label: Leaking / damaged compressor / grinding noise
results.explanation: Shaft seal failure leaks refrigerant and PAG oil. Internal piston seizure produces metallic rattling.
results.recommended_action: Replace AC compressor, receiver-drier, and flush system.

results.label: Intact and dry compressor casing
results.explanation: Compressor exterior integrity is intact.
results.recommended_action: Perform full AC pressure diagnostic scan.

repair_guide.title: AC Compressor Clutch & Belt Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Keep hands and loose clothing away from rotating serpentine belts and pulleys while engine is running.

steps.title: Visual Hub Check
steps.description: Turn AC button on and off inside cabin. Listen for crisp metallic "click" of clutch plate pulling in.

steps.title: Coil Resistance Check
steps.description: Unplug 1-wire or 2-wire connector to compressor and measure coil resistance (normal 3.0 to 4.5 ohms).

symptoms: AC cools at highway speed but warms up at idle
check_action: Inspect aluminum condenser behind front grille for bent cooling fins, leaf blockages, or stone punctures.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect AC condenser for debris or blockage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Condenser Fins for Road Debris, Bugs, and Mud
diagnosis_steps.description: Look through front bumper radiator grille with a flashlight at the thin aluminum heat exchanger.

results.label: Debris / blockage / bent fins present
results.explanation: Blocked airflow prevents hot high-pressure gas from condensing into liquid refrigerant.
results.recommended_action: Gently wash out bugs and dirt with low-pressure water hose and straighten fins.

results.label: Clean / clear condenser with good airflow
results.explanation: Air passages are open.
results.recommended_action: Check for refrigerant leaks with UV light.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check for leaks in AC condenser
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Condenser for Stone Punctures and Oily Spots
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect lower corners and face for dark damp oil spots where road gravel hit the thin tubes.

results.label: Leaking condenser (green UV stain or oily patch)
results.explanation: Stone strike puncture has vented all refrigerant gas to atmosphere.
results.recommended_action: Replace AC condenser and desiccant bag, then recharge system.

results.label: No leaks detected
results.explanation: Condenser tubes are sealed and pressurized.
results.recommended_action: Inspect evaporator, expansion valve, or compressor.

repair_guide.title: AC Condenser Cleaning & Leak Detection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not use a high-pressure pressure washer close to condenser; it will permanently fold aluminum fins.

steps.title: Wash Front Grille Fins
steps.description: Spray low pressure water from engine bay forward through radiator and condenser to push debris out.

steps.title: UV Inspection in Dark Area
steps.description: Shine UV light on condenser tubes to illuminate bright neon yellow/green leak tracer dye.

check_action: Inspect evaporator drain tube under car for water discharge and check cabin filter.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect AC evaporator for mold or mildew buildup
diagnosis_steps.title: Check for Bacterial / Fungal Buildup on Evaporator Core
diagnosis_steps.description: Smell air discharge on startup and inspect evaporator housing through cabin filter slot for mold.

results.label: Mold / mildew odor present
results.explanation: Condensation moisture trapped in dark evaporator chamber breeds mildew and fungal colonies.
results.recommended_action: Disinfect evaporator core with HVAC foam antimicrobial treatment and replace cabin filter.

results.label: Clean evaporator with fresh smelling airflow
results.explanation: Evaporator core is clean.
results.recommended_action: Check evaporator temperature sensor.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check AC evaporator temperature sensor
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Evaporator Anti-Frosting Temperature Sensor
diagnosis_steps.description: Test the thermistor mounted in the evaporator fins to ensure it prevents the core from freezing into a block of ice.

results.label: Faulty sensor (air flows cold then stops after 15 min)
results.explanation: Faulty sensor fails to cycle compressor, causing ice buildup that blocks all airflow through the core.
results.recommended_action: Replace evaporator thermistor probe.

results.label: Good sensor cycling compressor normally
results.explanation: Core temperature reading is accurate.
results.recommended_action: Check blower motor resistor or cabin filter.

repair_guide.title: AC Evaporator Foam Treatment & Drain Unclogging
repair_guide.safety_warning: Wear eye protection and keep car doors open when applying disinfectant foam.

steps.title: Locate Evaporator Drain Hose
steps.description: Under vehicle near firewall, check rubber drain nipple for dripping water while AC runs. Clear clogs with zip tie.

steps.title: Inject Disinfectant Foam
steps.description: Remove cabin filter, insert foam tube into evaporator box and spray entire can to dissolve bacterial biofilm.

symptoms: Hissing sound inside dashboard when AC turned on
check_action: Connect manifold pressure gauges to low and high side service ports to verify gas quantity.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check AC system pressure with gauge
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Static & Operating Refrigerant Pressures
diagnosis_steps.description: Connect low-side quick coupler to port (marked L). Normal resting static pressure is 50-80 PSI depending on ambient temperature.

results.label: Low pressure (below 25 PSI operating)
results.explanation: Refrigerant gas has leaked out slowly over time through O-rings, schrader valves, or hose crimps.
results.recommended_action: Vacuum test system, inject UV tracer dye, and refill factory refrigerant mass (e.g., 450g R134a).

results.label: Normal pressure (30-40 PSI low side, 150-200 PSI high side)
results.explanation: Refrigerant volume is optimal.
results.recommended_action: Inspect heater blend door actuator or cabin temperature sensor.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect for leaks in AC system
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Service Valves and Line Joints for Seepage
diagnosis_steps.description: Spray soapy water on service port schrader cores and examine all aluminum flange joints.

results.label: Leaking system (bubbles at valve or joints)
results.explanation: Rubber O-rings have dried out or schrader valve needle is loose.
results.recommended_action: Replace green HNBR rubber O-rings and tighten valve core with valve tool.

results.label: No leaks detected at ports
results.explanation: Service connections are sealed.
results.recommended_action: Check evaporator or condenser.

repair_guide.title: AC Pressure Quick Diagnostic
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never vent refrigerant gas into the atmosphere. It is illegal and harmful to the environment.

steps.title: Find Low Pressure Service Port
steps.description: Locate larger diameter aluminum pipe with plastic cap stamped "L".

steps.title: Snap On Quick Coupler
steps.description: Push coupler down until locking collar clicks, read dial on blue gauge.

symptoms: Windows fogging up easily in rain
check_action: Remove glove box access hatch and pull out filter pleats to check for dead leaves and black dust.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect and replace cabin air filter
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Cabin Microfilter Element
diagnosis_steps.description: Withdraw cabin filter from HVAC box behind glove box or beneath windshield cowl.

results.label: Dirty / clogged filter (choked with dust & debris)
results.explanation: Restricts blower motor airflow up to 70% and causes stale musty smells inside cabin.
results.recommended_action: Install a new activated carbon cabin pollen filter.

results.label: Clean / new white filter
results.explanation: Filter media allows full airflow.
results.recommended_action: Inspect cowl water drain and air intake.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check for debris in cabin air intake
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Windshield Cowl Mesh for Leaf Accumulation
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect plastic cowl beneath wiper arms for dead pine needles, leaves and clogged rainwater drain flaps.

results.label: Debris in air intake chamber
results.explanation: Debris holds rain moisture and rots, pulling damp odors directly into the ventilation blower.
results.recommended_action: Vacuum out cowl tray and flush drains with warm water.

results.label: Clear intake without obstruction
results.explanation: Fresh air path is clear.
results.recommended_action: Inspect blower motor fan wheel.

repair_guide.title: Cabin Air Filter DIY Replacement
tools_needed: Torx T20 screwdriver or hands only
repair_guide.safety_warning: Ensure directional airflow arrow on new filter points in the direction of airflow towards blower fan.

steps.title: Access Filter Housing Door
steps.description: Lower glovebox by unclipping side stops or unclip cover panel under driver/passenger dash.

steps.title: Slide Out Old Filter
steps.description: Pull old filter out smoothly so trapped leaves do not drop into blower motor squirrel cage.

steps.title: Insert New Activated Charcoal Filter
steps.description: Insert new filter paying attention to AIR FLOW arrow stamped on frame, reclip cover.

symptoms: Loud vibrating noise from HVAC system
check_action: Listen to blower fan under passenger glove compartment across all speeds 1 to 4.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test blower motor operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Test Blower Motor Electrical Response on Speed 4
diagnosis_steps.description: Turn fan switch to highest speed. Measure voltage at the 2-pin blower motor harness connector.

results.label: Motor not running despite 12V power present
results.explanation: Worn carbon brushes or burned motor windings prevent armature rotation.
results.recommended_action: Tap motor housing gently; if it spins temporarily, replace blower motor unit.

results.label: Motor running properly
results.explanation: Blower electric motor spins.
results.recommended_action: Check for physical cage imbalance or resistor failure.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect blower motor for debris or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Squirrel Cage Fan Wheel for Foreign Objects
diagnosis_steps.description: Drop motor out with 3 screws and inspect squirrel cage fan for trapped leaves, rodent nest, or broken blades.

results.label: Debris / damaged fan wheel present
results.explanation: A leaf or twig inside the cage causes intense rotational vibration and buzzing through the dashboard.
results.recommended_action: Clear debris and spin wheel by hand to verify smooth silence.

results.label: Clean and intact motor cage
results.explanation: Cage is balanced and clean.
results.recommended_action: Inspect blower motor resistor.

repair_guide.title: Blower Motor Removal & Cage Cleaning
repair_guide.safety_warning: Disconnect vehicle battery negative terminal before unclipping electrical plugs.

steps.title: Remove Passenger Footwell Trim
steps.description: Unclip plastic insulator shield above passenger footwell.

steps.title: Unscrew 3 Retaining Screws
steps.description: Unplug 2-pin electrical connector and remove the 3 screws securing blower motor flange.

steps.title: Clean Cage & Reinstall
steps.description: Dump out trapped debris, spin cage by hand to verify smooth bearings, and reinstall.

symptoms: HVAC fan only works on highest setting (Speed 4)
check_action: Test continuity across resistor pack terminals and inspect thermal fuse.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test blower motor resistor continuity
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Resistor Continuity with Multimeter
diagnosis_steps.description: Check resistance values across stepped pins on the resistor pack or electronic PWM final stage module.

results.label: Resistor failure / open circuit on lower speeds
results.explanation: Thermal cutoff fuse blown because lower speeds use resistive coils that drop voltage through heat.
results.recommended_action: Replace blower motor resistor pack and inspect cabin filter for restricted airflow.

results.label: Resistor working properly with normal continuity
results.explanation: Resistance steps are intact.
results.recommended_action: Inspect dashboard rotary fan switch or wiring harness.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect resistor for overheating or burn marks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Wiring Connector for Melted Plastic or Heat Discoloration
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine harness plug going into resistor module for melted terminals due to excessive current draw.

results.label: Overheated / melted connector pins
results.explanation: High electrical resistance at terminal pins melts plastic plug, causing intermittent fan cutouts.
results.recommended_action: Splice in a replacement pigtail harness connector and new resistor.

results.label: Good condition resistor and clean plug
results.explanation: Electrical terminals show no signs of overheating.
results.recommended_action: Test dashboard climate control panel switch.

repair_guide.title: Blower Motor Resistor Quick Replacement
repair_guide.safety_warning: Resistor pack gets extremely hot during operation. Allow 10 minutes to cool before touching.

steps.title: Locate Resistor in HVAC Duct
steps.description: Mounted into the air duct near the blower motor to keep it cooled by incoming air.

steps.title: Unplug and Replace
steps.description: Depress locking tab, pull wiring connector, remove 2 mounting screws, and insert new resistor.

symptoms: Sweet syrupy odor from engine bay
check_action: Visually check translucent expansion tank level and inspect for cracks or cap seal degradation.
safety_warning: NEVER open the coolant reservoir cap while engine is hot! Scalding steam and boiling liquid will erupt under pressure.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check coolant level and condition
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Expansion Tank Fluid Level & Color Cold
diagnosis_steps.description: With engine completely cold, observe fluid meniscus relative to MIN and MAX marks. Fluid should be bright pink, yellow, or blue.

results.label: Low / empty / muddy brown coolant
results.explanation: Fluid loss starves the engine cylinder head of heat transfer liquid, causing rapid catastrophic overheating.
results.recommended_action: Refill with premixed 50/50 OAT coolant and perform cooling system pressure test.

results.label: Sufficient & clean coolant between MIN and MAX
results.explanation: Reservoir fluid volume is adequate.
results.recommended_action: Proceed to thermostat and radiator fan checks.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect reservoir for cracks or leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Plastic Tank Seams and Pressurized Cap
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine the molded ultrasonic weld seam around the middle of the plastic bottle and the hose nipples for hairline cracks.

results.label: Cracked / leaking reservoir or venting cap
results.explanation: Plastic becomes brittle from heat cycles. A leaking cap fails to hold the 1.2 to 1.4 bar pressure required to raise boiling point.
results.recommended_action: Replace expansion tank and pressure relief cap.

results.label: Intact reservoir and tight cap seal
results.explanation: Tank holds pressure.
results.recommended_action: Inspect radiator, water pump, and thermostat.

repair_guide.title: Coolant Level Top-up & Expansion Tank Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Wait at least 45 minutes after driving before opening the cooling system cap.

steps.title: Confirm Engine Cold
steps.description: Touch upper radiator hose; if it feels hot or pressurized like a firm tire, wait for it to cool.

steps.title: Slowly Unscrew Cap with Towel
steps.description: Place thick towel over cap and turn counterclockwise to first detent to release any residual pressure hiss, then remove.

steps.title: Fill to MAX Mark
steps.description: Pour correct specification coolant to MAX line. Do not overfill, as expansion space is required when hot.

check_action: Pressure test cooling system to 15 PSI (1 bar) with hand pump and inspect for drips.
safety_warning: Operating an engine without coolant will warp the aluminum cylinder head within minutes.

diagnosis_steps.step: Pressure test cooling system
diagnosis_steps.title: Pressurize Cold Cooling System with Hand Tester
diagnosis_steps.description: Attach radiator pressure tester adapter to expansion tank, pump to 15 PSI / 1.0 bar, and watch the gauge needle for 10 minutes.

results.label: Gauge needle drops (leaking system)
results.explanation: Pressure decay indicates an active external hose/radiator leak or internal head gasket breach.
results.recommended_action: Look for dripping liquid beneath vehicle while system is under test pressure.

results.label: Pressure holds steady (no leaks detected)
results.explanation: Circuit is hermetically sealed under static pressure.
results.recommended_action: Check for high-temperature dynamic leak under load or thermostat failure.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect radiator, hoses, and water pump for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Locate Active Coolant Seepage Point
diagnosis_steps.description: Trace hoses, thermostat housing plastic flange, water pump weep hole, and radiator side tanks for drips.

results.label: Leaking component found (radiator, hose, or water pump)
results.explanation: Identified the leaking component responsible for coolant loss.
results.recommended_action: Replace the defective hose, clamp, or water pump assembly.

results.label: All external components dry and intact
results.explanation: External circuit is tight. If coolant is vanishing, internal head gasket leak suspected.
results.recommended_action: Perform chemical combustion gas test in expansion tank.

repair_guide.title: Cooling Leak Tracing & Puddle Identification
repair_guide.safety_warning: Coolant has a sweet taste and is extremely toxic to pets. Clean all spills immediately.

steps.title: Place White Cardboard Under Engine
steps.description: Park on clean pavement, slide cardboard under engine bay, and let sit overnight to spot drip locations.

steps.title: Identify Fluid
steps.description: Coolant feels slippery like watered syrup with sweet smell, unlike clear water (AC condensation) or black oil.

symptoms: Engine runs too cold on highway
check_action: Feel upper and lower radiator hoses while engine warms up to check if thermostat valve opens.
safety_warning: A thermostat stuck closed prevents coolant from circulating to the radiator, causing rapid overheating.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check radiator for blockage or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Radiator Core and Airflow Blockages
diagnosis_steps.description: Ensure radiator aluminum core is not packed with mud, leaves, or plastic bags.

results.label: Blocked / damaged radiator core
results.explanation: External debris prevents ambient air from cooling the engine coolant passing through tubes.
results.recommended_action: Clean debris from radiator core with low-pressure water.

results.label: Clear & intact radiator core
results.explanation: Air passages are open.
results.recommended_action: Proceed to thermostat cycling test.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test thermostat operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Test Thermostat Opening by Touching Radiator Hoses
diagnosis_steps.description: Start cold engine. Upper hose should stay cold until engine reaches 88°C - 92°C, then suddenly become hot.

results.label: Faulty thermostat (stuck closed: upper hose cold while engine boiling)
results.explanation: Thermostat wax pellet has failed, trapping hot coolant inside engine block without radiator circulation.
results.recommended_action: Replace thermostat assembly and gasket, then bleed air from cooling circuit.

results.label: Thermostat functioning properly (hose warms up smoothly at ~90°C)
results.explanation: Thermostat valve opens and closes at specified temperature threshold.
results.recommended_action: Check cooling fan motor and water pump impeller.

repair_guide.title: Thermostat Replacement & Air Bleeding
repair_guide.safety_warning: Air pockets in the cylinder head can cause hot spots and engine failure. Always bleed air properly.

steps.title: Drain 2 Liters of Coolant
steps.description: Open radiator drain petcock to lower coolant level below the thermostat housing.

steps.title: Unbolt Thermostat Housing
steps.description: Remove 2 to 3 bolts securing the water neck, pull out old thermostat, note jiggle pin orientation.

steps.title: Install New Unit with Jiggle Pin at 12 O’clock
steps.description: Fit new rubber O-ring seal, torque bolts to 10 Nm, refill and open air bleed screws until solid stream flows.

check_action: Touch both heater inlet and outlet hoses at firewall; both should be equally hot when engine is at operating temperature.
safety_warning: A leaking heater core sprays hot coolant vapor into the passenger compartment, causing sudden window fogging.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect heater core for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Passenger Carpet and HVAC Housing for Coolant Stains
diagnosis_steps.description: Feel underneath passenger footwell carpet near center console for damp green/pink sticky residue.

results.label: Leaking heater core (wet carpet & greasy windshield fog)
results.explanation: The mini-radiator inside the dashboard has developed a tube crack or tank leak.
results.recommended_action: Replace heater core assembly (or bypass temporarily with a U-hose connector).

results.label: No leaks detected in cabin
results.explanation: Heater core is dry and leak-free.
results.recommended_action: Check coolant flow circulation through core.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check coolant flow through heater core
diagnosis_steps.title: Compare Temperatures of Both Firewall Heater Hoses
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine at 90°C with heater blower ON, touch both rubber hoses entering the passenger firewall.

results.label: Restricted flow (inlet hose burning hot, outlet hose cold)
results.explanation: Heater core tubes are clogged with scale, rust or stop-leak additive, starving the cabin of heat.
results.recommended_action: Perform bidirectional chemical flush of the heater core using garden hose adapter.

results.label: Good coolant flow (both hoses uniformly hot)
results.explanation: Coolant circulation through core is unimpeded.
results.recommended_action: Inspect electric blend door actuator inside dashboard.

repair_guide.title: Heater Core Reverse Flush Procedure
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not use excessive mains water pressure; aluminum heater core tubes are thin and fragile.

steps.title: Disconnect Both Heater Hoses at Firewall
steps.description: Squeeze spring clamps, gently twist hoses off aluminum heater core spigots.

steps.title: Reverse Flush with Water
steps.description: Connect water hose to OUTLET pipe and drain hose to INLET pipe. Flush backwards into bucket until water runs completely clear.

symptoms: Engine overheating in traffic / at idle
Fan does not spin when temperature rises
check_action: Switch AC ON to verify if radiator fan turns on automatically, and test fan relay.
safety_warning: Electric cooling fans can start automatically at any time even with key off. Keep hands clear.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test radiator fan operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Command Fan On by Engaging AC Compressor
diagnosis_steps.description: With engine idling, switch AC to ON. On modern vehicles, this automatically triggers radiator fan speed 1.

results.label: Fan not spinning
results.explanation: Electric fan motor failure, blown 40A high-power fuse, or open cooling fan relay.
results.recommended_action: Check 40A fuse and supply 12V direct test power to fan motor plug.

results.label: Fan operates correctly with strong airflow
results.explanation: Fan motor and basic drive circuit work.
results.recommended_action: Check engine coolant temperature sensor (ECT) signal.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect radiator fan motor and relay
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Fan Relay and Motor Resistor Pack
diagnosis_steps.description: Locate cooling fan relay in underhood fuse box. Swap with identical horn/defrost relay to test.

results.label: Faulty motor / relay or burned dropping resistor
results.explanation: Burned relay contacts or open low-speed resistor prevent fan from engaging when temperature climbs.
results.recommended_action: Replace fan relay or fan shroud resistor pack.

results.label: Motor and relay functioning properly
results.explanation: Fan electrical controls are functional.
results.recommended_action: Check water pump and thermostat.

repair_guide.title: Radiator Fan Motor Direct Power Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Disconnect main battery before probing fuse box terminals.

steps.title: Unplug Fan Harness
steps.description: Locate 2-pin connector on fan motor shroud, disconnect.

steps.title: Apply 12V Battery Power
steps.description: Touch fused 12V lead to positive pin and ground to negative pin. If fan does not spin at full speed, motor brushes are worn out.

symptoms: Hose collapses flat when revving engine
check_action: Squeeze upper and lower radiator hoses cold; check for spongy texture, hard brittle spots, or clamp cuts.
safety_warning: A ruptured upper radiator hose instantly dumps entire cooling volume directly over the hot engine.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect radiator hoses for damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Squeeze Hoses to Inspect Rubber Condition
diagnosis_steps.description: Check along full length of upper and lower radiator hoses for bulging, softening from oil contamination, or dry rotting.

results.label: Damaged, soft, swollen or cracked hoses found
results.explanation: Internal fabric reinforcement degraded. Engine oil dripping from valve cover softens EPDM rubber rapidly.
results.recommended_action: Replace both upper and lower radiator hoses and install fresh worm-gear or constant-tension clamps.

results.label: Hoses are firm, pliable and in good condition
results.explanation: Rubber hose walls are structurally sound.
results.recommended_action: Inspect hose neck clamp connections.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check hose connections for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Metal / Plastic Radiator Spigot Joints for Crusty Residue
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine ends where hoses clamp onto radiator and thermostat housing for dried white/pink crystalline coolant deposits.

results.label: Leaking connections / crusty buildup around clamps
results.explanation: Weakened spring clamp or cracked plastic radiator hose neck weeping coolant under thermal expansion.
results.recommended_action: Clean corrosion from spigot, install new hose and stainless steel hose clamp.

results.label: No leaks detected at joints
results.explanation: Connections are tight and dry.
results.recommended_action: Inspect water pump and radiator core.

repair_guide.title: Radiator Hose Replacement & Clamp Tightening
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not overtighten screw clamps on plastic radiator necks; plastic can crush easily.

steps.title: Drain Coolant Below Hose Level
steps.description: Place pan under radiator drain cock and drain enough coolant to prevent spills.

steps.title: Loosen Clamps & Twist Off
steps.description: Slide clamps back. Gently twist hose back and forth to break seal before pulling.

symptoms: Coolant leak near front of engine
Grinding or whining noise from timing cover
check_action: Inspect water pump shaft weep hole for coolant drips and check pulley for bearing wobble/play.
safety_warning: If water pump is driven by timing belt, bearing seizure can snap the belt and destroy engine valves.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect water pump for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Water Pump Weep Hole for Coolant Stains
diagnosis_steps.description: Use a dental inspection mirror or flashlight to look beneath the water pump pulley hub at the small weep drain hole.

results.label: Leaking pump (wet coolant or crusty trail from weep hole)
results.explanation: Internal mechanical carbon-ceramic face seal has failed, allowing pressurized coolant to escape through the bearing chamber.
results.recommended_action: Replace water pump (and timing belt kit if timing-belt driven).

results.label: Dry weep hole with no leaks detected
results.explanation: Mechanical shaft seal is holding pressure.
results.recommended_action: Check water pump pulley bearing play.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test water pump for proper operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Impeller Circulation & Pulley Play with Belt Removed
diagnosis_steps.description: Wiggle water pump pulley with belt off to detect shaft play, and observe return flow into expansion tank at 2500 RPM.

results.label: Faulty pump (loose wobbly bearing or plastic impeller slipping on shaft)
results.explanation: Bearing wear or cracked plastic impeller frees the shaft from pumping, halting all coolant circulation.
results.recommended_action: Install new water pump featuring a durable metal impeller.

results.label: Pump working correctly with steady return stream
results.explanation: Impeller is circulating coolant normally.
results.recommended_action: Inspect thermostat and radiator fan.

repair_guide.title: Water Pump Inspection & Circulation Verification
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always check water pump whenever replacing timing belt to avoid duplicate labor costs.

steps.title: Observe Overflow Return Stream
steps.description: Remove expansion tank cap cold, start engine, have helper rev to 2500 RPM. A steady continuous stream should shoot into the tank neck.

steps.title: Check Pulley Bearing Free Play
steps.description: With engine off, grab water pump pulley firmly with both hands and wiggle up/down. Any audible click or play means bearings are finished.

check_action: Use a mechanic stethoscope to listen for regular rhythmic clicking on each injector body.
safety_warning: A leaking injector stuck open can wash cylinder oil away or cause hydraulic engine lock (hydrolock).

diagnosis_steps.step: Test fuel injector spray pattern
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Injector Spray Pattern & Balance Rates
diagnosis_steps.description: Perform injector balance test or remove fuel rail with injectors attached and crank into graduated test beakers.

results.label: Irregular / dripping / clogged spray pattern
results.explanation: Carbon deposits choke injector pintle nozzles, resulting in fuel droplets instead of fine atomized mist.
results.recommended_action: Ultrasonic clean injectors or replace defective fuel injector.

results.label: Uniform conical atomized spray pattern
results.explanation: Fuel atomization is optimal.
results.recommended_action: Check electrical coil resistance and harness.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect injector for leaks or clogs
diagnosis_steps.title: Test Injector Solenoid Resistance with Multimeter
diagnosis_steps.description: Unplug electrical harness and measure coil resistance across the 2 pins (spec: 12-16 ohms high-Z, 2-4 ohms low-Z).

results.label: Open circuit / out of tolerance / external O-ring leak
results.explanation: Burned solenoid coil prevents valve from opening, producing an immediate cylinder misfire (P0300/P030X).
results.recommended_action: Replace the fuel injector and install new Viton O-rings with clean silicone lubricant.

results.label: In-tolerance coil resistance & clean injector
results.explanation: Injector solenoid is electrically functional.
results.recommended_action: Check spark plugs, ignition coils, and fuel pressure.

repair_guide.title: Fuel Injector Stethoscope Listening & Resistance Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Fuel rail operates under high pressure (3 to 5 bar for petrol, over 1500 bar for common-rail diesel). Relieve pressure first.

steps.title: Stethoscope Click Test
steps.description: Place tip of screwdriver on metal body of injector while engine idles. Put ear to handle. You should hear sharp, rhythmic "tick-tick-tick".

steps.title: Compare All Cylinders
steps.description: Move to each cylinder. A silent injector or dull thud indicates a stuck or non-energized injector.

check_action: Pull vacuum hose off fuel pressure regulator; if raw gasoline drips out, internal diaphragm is torn.
safety_warning: A ruptured regulator diaphragm dumps raw fuel directly into the engine intake manifold through vacuum port.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test fuel pressure regulator operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Vacuum Port for Raw Gasoline Presence
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine off, pull small rubber vacuum hose off the regulator snout and inspect for liquid fuel or smell.

results.label: Regulator malfunction (liquid fuel in vacuum hose)
results.explanation: Torn internal rubber diaphragm allows pressurized fuel to be sucked straight into intake manifold, running extremely rich.
results.recommended_action: Replace fuel pressure regulator immediately.

results.label: Dry vacuum port with no trace of fuel
results.explanation: Diaphragm is intact and holding seal.
results.recommended_action: Measure line pressure with mechanical gauge.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check fuel pressure at regulator
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Fuel Rail Pressure at Schrader Valve
diagnosis_steps.description: Screw fuel pressure test gauge onto fuel rail test port. Key ON engine OFF, verify pressure against manufacturer spec (e.g. 3.5 bar).

results.label: Abnormally high or low pressure
results.explanation: Internal spring weak (too low) or return line orifice jammed shut (excessive pressure causes rich codes).
results.recommended_action: Replace regulator and clean return line.

results.label: Correct specification pressure holding steady
results.explanation: Pressure regulation is within OEM tolerances.
results.recommended_action: Check fuel pump volume flow and filter.

repair_guide.title: Fuel Regulator Vacuum Check & Pressure Gauge Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Cover fuel rail test port with shop rag when screwing on gauge to catch escaping fuel spray.

steps.title: Sniff Vacuum Line
steps.description: Pull small vacuum tube off regulator; any gasoline wetness proves immediate internal diaphragm failure.

steps.title: Observe Pressure Drop After Engine Shut-off
steps.description: Turn engine off. Pressure should stay above 2.0 bar for at least 15 minutes. Rapid drop indicates leaking regulator or check valve.

symptoms: Car cranks but will not start
check_action: Listen for 2-second hum from under rear seat when turning ignition to ON (pos II), and test fuel pressure.
safety_warning: Never test fuel pump wiring near open fuel containers or spilled gasoline. Disconnect battery.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test fuel pump pressure
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Fuel Delivery Pressure & Volume
diagnosis_steps.description: Connect fuel gauge to fuel rail. Read static prime pressure and flow volume into measuring bottle (min 1L per minute).

results.label: Low pressure / no fuel flow / pressure drops under load
results.explanation: Worn pump motor commutator, burned brushes, or clogged in-tank sock filter.
results.recommended_action: Replace in-tank fuel pump assembly and fuel filter.

results.label: Normal pressure and strong volume flow
results.explanation: Pump delivers correct flow and pressure head.
results.recommended_action: Check fuel pump relay and tank level sender.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect fuel pump for leaks or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Fuel Pump Flange & Electrical Harness Under Rear Seat
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove rear seat cushion, pop open metal access hatch, and inspect electrical plug for melted pins.

results.label: Leaking flange / melted electrical connector
results.explanation: High current draw through corroded terminals melts top flange socket, causing intermittent pump shutdown.
results.recommended_action: Replace fuel pump unit and splice new wiring pigtail connector.

results.label: Clean, intact and sealed pump housing
results.explanation: Flange seals and electrical connector are intact.
results.recommended_action: Check fuel pump relay in engine bay.

repair_guide.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Priming & Sound Verification
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not smoke or use open flames around fuel tank access port.

steps.title: Prime Sound Test
steps.description: Remove fuel filler cap. Have helper turn ignition ON (do not crank). Place ear near filler neck. You should hear a distinct 2-second electric hum.

steps.title: Check Pump Relay
steps.description: If completely silent, locate FUEL PUMP relay in fuse panel, verify relay click, and check 15A/20A fuse.

symptoms: Visible fuel leak under vehicle after fill-up
Hissing sound when opening gas cap
check_action: Inspect plastic/metal fuel tank, filler pipe neck for rust holes, and check gas cap rubber seal gasket.
safety_warning: Liquid fuel leaks or heavy vapor accumulation under vehicle create extreme fire hazard.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect fuel tank for leaks or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Tank Shell, Seams, and Filler Neck
diagnosis_steps.description: Lift vehicle and visually inspect tank straps, metal filler neck pipe behind rear wheel liner, and tank bottom for rust or scrape gouges.

results.label: Leaking / damaged / rusted tank or filler neck
results.explanation: Road salt rots steel filler pipes, allowing fuel to splash out during fueling and moisture into fuel.
results.recommended_action: Replace rusted filler neck or damaged fuel tank.

results.label: Tank and filler neck in good condition
results.explanation: Tank body is intact and sealed.
results.recommended_action: Inspect fuel cap seal and EVAP lines.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check fuel filler cap for seal
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Gas Cap Rubber O-Ring Gasket
diagnosis_steps.description: Unscrew gas cap and inspect rubber sealing ring for cracking, deformation, or loose ratchet clicking mechanism.

results.label: Loose / broken / cracked cap seal
results.explanation: Vents fuel vapor into atmosphere, triggering Check Engine EVAP leak code (P0440 / P0455).
results.recommended_action: Replace gas cap with OEM locking cap.

results.label: Cap seals properly with firm ratchet click
results.explanation: Gas cap seals vapor tightly.
results.recommended_action: Check charcoal canister and purge solenoid valve.

repair_guide.title: Gas Cap Seal & Filler Neck Rust Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Keep car parked away from ignition sources while inspecting fuel components.

steps.title: Examine Gas Cap Rubber Gasket
steps.description: Remove cap and look at black rubber gasket ring. If split, flattened or cracked, vapor will escape.

steps.title: Inspect Filler Pipe Behind Wheel
steps.description: Look inside rear right/left wheel well where tires throw road grit directly against metal fuel pipe.

check_action: Check maintenance history (replace every 40,000 to 60,000 km) and test fuel flow resistance.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect fuel filter for clogs or debris
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Fuel Filter Service Mileage and Flow Restriction
diagnosis_steps.description: Locate inline fuel filter under vehicle floor pan or in engine compartment (diesel). Check service records.

results.label: Clogged / dirty filter with black sediment
results.explanation: Trapped dirt and water create a severe restriction, starving high-RPM fuel demand.
results.recommended_action: Replace fuel filter canister and drain water trap if diesel.

results.label: Clean filter recently replaced
results.explanation: Fuel filter flow capacity is adequate.
results.recommended_action: Check fuel pump pressure and fuel injectors.

diagnosis_steps.step: Replace fuel filter if necessary
diagnosis_steps.title: Verify Quick-Disconnect Fittings and Direction Arrow
diagnosis_steps.description: Ensure filter is installed with directional arrow pointing toward engine, and disconnects are clicked firmly.

results.label: Replace filter (exceeded 60,000 km or restricted)
results.explanation: Preventive replacement restores full unrestricted flow to fuel rail.
results.recommended_action: Install fresh OEM filter.

results.label: Filter in good condition
results.explanation: Filter is within service lifespan.
results.recommended_action: Test fuel pump.

repair_guide.title: Inline Fuel Filter Replacement
repair_guide.safety_warning: Wear eye protection. Residual fuel pressure will spray when lines are released.

steps.title: Depressurize Fuel System
steps.description: Pull fuel pump fuse, crank engine until it stalls to deplete line pressure.

steps.title: Release Quick Fittings
steps.description: Squeeze plastic tabs or insert release tool into collar, catch draining fuel in pan.

steps.title: Install New Filter with Correct Flow Direction
steps.description: Orient arrow pointing toward front of car, push connectors until positive click is heard.

symptoms: High-pitched slapping noise under timing cover
check_action: Pull back top plastic timing cover inspection window to inspect belt teeth, tension, and fraying.
safety_warning: On interference engines, a broken timing belt causes pistons to smash into open valves, destroying the engine.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect timing belt for wear or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Timing Belt Teeth and Backing for Cracking or Oil Soaking
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove top timing cover clips. Examine rubber teeth, looking for missing teeth, shredded cords, or oil contamination.

results.label: Worn / damaged / oil-soaked / stripped belt teeth
results.explanation: Degraded rubber can slip teeth on camshaft sprocket or snap entirely during cranking.
results.recommended_action: Replace timing belt, tensioner pulley, idlers, and water pump immediately. Do not crank engine!

results.label: Belt in good condition with crisp teeth and clean backing
results.explanation: Belt physical integrity appears intact.
results.recommended_action: Check timing mark synchronization.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check timing marks for alignment
diagnosis_steps.title: Verify Crankshaft and Camshaft TDC Timing Alignment Marks
diagnosis_steps.description: Rotate engine by hand to Top Dead Center (TDC) on cylinder 1. Check if camshaft and crankshaft index marks align precisely.

results.label: Misaligned timing marks (belt has jumped 1 or more teeth)
results.explanation: Jumped timing causes valve timing overlap error, loss of cylinder compression, and backfiring.
results.recommended_action: Re-align timing marks with locking tools, install new timing belt kit and tensioner.

results.label: Properly aligned timing marks
results.explanation: Engine mechanical synchronization is correct.
results.recommended_action: Check ignition spark, crankshaft sensor, and fuel supply.

repair_guide.title: Timing Belt Visual Inspection & Tension Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: NEVER turn the engine over using the camshaft bolt; only rotate the crankshaft bolt clockwise.

steps.title: Unclip Upper Timing Cover
steps.description: Remove the 2 or 3 bolts on upper plastic timing shroud and pull outward to expose belt.

steps.title: Check Belt Deflection
steps.description: Twist belt with thumb and forefinger between sprockets; it should not twist beyond 90 degrees under moderate pressure.

check_action: Inspect ribbed belt surface for micro-cracks, glazing, fraying cords, and check automatic tensioner mark.
safety_warning: A snapped serpentine belt immediately cuts alternator charging, water pump circulation, and power steering assist.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect drive belt for cuts or wear
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect V-Ribbed Belt Surface for Cracks & Glazing
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine underside multi-V ribs with flashlight. Count cracks: more than 3 cracks per inch indicates imminent failure.

results.label: Cut / worn / glazed / shredded belt
results.explanation: Glazed belt slips on alternator and water pump pulleys, causing loud squealing and loss of charging.
results.recommended_action: Replace serpentine belt and check all idler pulleys for bearing play.

results.label: Belt in good condition with clean flexible rubber
results.explanation: Belt rubber is sound.
results.recommended_action: Check belt tension and pulley alignment.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check belt tension and alignment
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Automatic Belt Tensioner & Pulley Coplanarity
diagnosis_steps.description: Observe automatic tensioner arm while engine idles. It should remain steady without aggressive bouncing or chatter.

results.label: Loose / misaligned belt or chattering tensioner
results.explanation: Weak internal tensioner spring or seized decoupler alternator pulley (OAP) causes belt flutter and thrown belts.
results.recommended_action: Replace automatic tensioner assembly and alternator one-way freewheel pulley.

results.label: Properly tensioned and aligned belt running true
results.explanation: Tension and alignment are correct.
results.recommended_action: If squealing persists, check alternator or AC compressor bearings.

repair_guide.title: Serpentine Belt Replacement & Tensioner Relieving
tools_needed: Serpentine belt tool / 15mm or 16mm long wrench
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always sketch or photograph belt routing around pulleys before releasing tension.

steps.title: Rotate Tensioner Bolt
steps.description: Place wrench on tensioner pulley center bolt, pull in direction to compress internal spring.

steps.title: Slip Belt Off Alternator Pulley
steps.description: While holding tensioner back, slide belt off easily accessible top pulley, then ease tensioner back.

steps.title: Thread New Belt & Release
steps.description: Route new belt following exact diagram, lever tensioner, slip over last pulley, verify belt sits in all grooves.

check_action: Inspect intercooler rubber boost hoses for splits and check wastegate actuator vacuum movement.
safety_warning: A catastrophic turbo compressor wheel breakup can send aluminum fragments into engine cylinders.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check boost pressure with gauge / OBD scanner
diagnosis_steps.title: Compare Specified vs Actual Manifold Boost Pressure
diagnosis_steps.description: Read live OBD data for MAP (Manifold Absolute Pressure) during wide open throttle acceleration in 3rd gear.

results.label: Low boost pressure (underboost condition P0299)
results.explanation: Charge air leak in boost hoses, stuck open wastegate, or seized variable geometry vanes (VNT).
results.recommended_action: Smoke test charge air piping and test wastegate actuator solenoid valve.

results.label: Normal boost pressure tracking requested target
results.explanation: Turbo pressure build-up matches ECU target.
results.recommended_action: Inspect intercooler and MAF sensor.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect intercooler for leaks or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Intercooler End Tanks and Silicone Boost Hoses
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine lower front intercooler for split plastic end caps or oily residue indicating boost pressure leaks.

results.label: Leaking / split / damaged intercooler or ruptured boost hose
results.explanation: Boost air vents to atmosphere, causing loss of power, whooshing air noise under load, and excessive fuel smoke.
results.recommended_action: Replace punctured intercooler or split reinforced boost hose.

results.label: Intact intercooler holding full boost pressure
results.explanation: Charge air piping is airtight.
results.recommended_action: Check turbo shaft radial/axial play.

repair_guide.title: Boost Hose Smoke Test & Turbo Shaft Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not touch turbocharger turbine housing immediately after driving; temperatures exceed 600°C.

steps.title: Feel Along Boost Hoses
steps.description: Examine thick rubber boost pipes between turbo, intercooler, and intake manifold. Feel for splits on undersides.

steps.title: Wiggle Compressor Shaft
steps.description: Remove air intake hose to expose turbo compressor wheel. Gently wiggle shaft; slight radial play (oil cushion) is normal, zero axial play allowed.

symptoms: Glow plug indicator light stays on / flashing
check_action: Measure electrical resistance of each glow plug with multimeter (normal: 0.5 to 1.5 ohms).
safety_warning: Glow plugs can seize in aluminum cylinder heads. Always soak with penetrating oil and use a torque wrench to avoid snapping.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test glow plug resistance
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Individual Glow Plug Internal Resistance
diagnosis_steps.description: Disconnect wiring harness bus bar, attach multimeter negative to engine block and positive to glow plug terminal.

results.label: High resistance / infinite ohms (open circuit burned element)
results.explanation: Heating coil burned open, preventing cylinder preheating needed for cold diesel auto-ignition.
results.recommended_action: Replace all glow plugs as a complete matched set.

results.label: Normal low resistance (0.6 - 1.2 ohms)
results.explanation: Heating element is intact.
results.recommended_action: Check glow plug relay and preheat control timer module.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect glow plug for carbon buildup
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Glow Plug Tips for Carbon Blistering or Melting
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine removed glow plug tips for excessive black crust, swollen tips, or erosion from faulty fuel injector spray.

results.label: Heavy carbon buildup / eroded or swollen tip
results.explanation: Dripping fuel injector or excessive EGR soot coats plug, insulating heat from combustion chamber.
results.recommended_action: Clean threaded bores with reamer tool and check fuel injectors.

results.label: Clean plug tip with light grey ash
results.explanation: Combustion conditions are healthy.
results.recommended_action: Check glow plug power feed relay.

repair_guide.title: Glow Plug Multimeter Testing Without Removal
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never apply direct 12V test battery power to modern 4.4V or 7V low-voltage fast glow plugs; they will explode instantly.

steps.title: Unclip Electrical Connectors
steps.description: Pull electrical rubber caps off each glow plug head.

steps.title: Set Meter to Lowest Ohms (200Ω)
steps.description: Touch red lead to top terminal and black lead to clean metal engine ground. A reading over 2 ohms or OL means plug is burned.

symptoms: Clunking noise when accelerating or shifting gears
Vibrations felt in cabin at idle
check_action: Inspect hydraulic / rubber mounts for tears, hydraulic oil leaks, or excessive engine rock when revving.
safety_warning: A completely broken engine mount allows engine to shift, stressing radiator hoses, wiring, and exhaust flex pipes.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect engine mounts for wear or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Rubber Bushings and Hydraulic Fluid Chambers
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine right passenger side hydraulic mount and lower rear dogbone torque mount for torn rubber and black fluid stains.

results.label: Worn / torn rubber or leaking hydraulic mount oil
results.explanation: Internal hydraulic damping fluid has leaked out or rubber web is severed, transferring harsh engine vibration directly to chassis.
results.recommended_action: Replace defective engine mount and lower torque reaction dogbone mount.

results.label: Mounts in good condition with firm pliable rubber
results.explanation: Rubber and hydraulic dampening are intact.
results.recommended_action: Check mounting bolts and exhaust hangers.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check mounting bolts for tightness
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Engine Mount Retaining Bolts & Bracket Torque
diagnosis_steps.description: Verify with a torque wrench that all subframe and engine bracket mounting bolts are tight.

results.label: Loose or sheared mounting bolts
results.explanation: Loose bolts allow aluminum bracket to clunk against steel chassis unibody rail during acceleration.
results.recommended_action: Torque bolts to specification or replace with new stretch bolts.

results.label: Tight bolts torqued to specification
results.explanation: Bolts are secure.
results.recommended_action: Inspect suspension control arm bushings.

repair_guide.title: Engine Mount Rocking & Power Braking Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never place jack directly against bare aluminum oil pan without thick wooden block to distribute load.

steps.title: Visual Rocking Inspection
steps.description: Have a helper sit in car with parking brake ON. Put in 1st gear (or Drive), tap accelerator briefly while watching engine. More than 2-3 cm rock indicates bad mount.

steps.title: Pry Bar Test
steps.description: Gently lever between mount bracket and chassis rail with pry bar. Free sloppy movement indicates severed rubber core.

symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay
Oil pooling in spark plug wells
check_action: Inspect seam between cylinder head and valve cover for wet oil seepage dripping onto hot exhaust manifold.
safety_warning: Oil dripping onto hot exhaust manifold creates white smoke and fire risk in engine compartment.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect valve cover gasket for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Valve Cover Perimeter & Spark Plug Wells for Oil
diagnosis_steps.description: Pull ignition coils out of spark plug tubes. If rubber coil boots come out dripping in engine oil, internal tube seals have failed.

results.label: Leaking gasket / oil in spark plug tubes
results.explanation: Hardened rubber gasket loses elasticity from heat cycles, leaking oil down engine block and into spark plug wells.
results.recommended_action: Replace valve cover gasket set (including spark plug tube seals) and clean wells.

results.label: Dry perimeter with good gasket seal
results.explanation: Valve cover perimeter is oil tight.
results.recommended_action: Check camshaft oil seals or PCV breather hose.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check valve cover bolts for tightness
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Valve Cover Bolt Torque
diagnosis_steps.description: Verify small 10mm bolts are torqued evenly (typically 8 to 10 Nm).

results.label: Loose bolts or cracked plastic cover
results.explanation: Vibrations loosen bolts over time, or overtightening cracks the plastic valve cover.
results.recommended_action: Torque bolts crisscross from center outward or replace warped plastic valve cover.

results.label: Tight bolts torqued evenly
results.explanation: Bolts are secure.
results.recommended_action: Check oil filler cap gasket.

repair_guide.title: Valve Cover Gasket Replacement & Surface Prep
repair_guide.safety_warning: Clean cylinder head mating surface thoroughly. Do not drop dirt or old gasket flakes into exposed camshafts.

steps.title: Disconnect Breather Hoses & Coils
steps.description: Unclip spark plug coils, unbolt ground straps, and pull PCV breather hoses off cover.

steps.title: Lift Cover & Scrape Clean
steps.description: Remove perimeter bolts, lift cover. Clean mating surfaces with brake cleaner.

steps.title: Apply RTV at Timing Corners
steps.description: Place a dab of RTV silicone sealant at the camshaft arch joints, install new gasket, and torque to 9 Nm.

symptoms: Low oil pressure warning light on
Loud hydraulic lifter clatter at idle
check_action: Screw mechanical oil pressure gauge into pressure switch port to measure actual bar/PSI at idle and 3000 RPM.
safety_warning: STOP ENGINE IMMEDIATELY if red oil pressure light flashes. Operating without oil pressure ruins crankshaft bearings in seconds.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test oil pressure with gauge
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure True Engine Oil Pressure with Mechanical Gauge
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove oil pressure sensor switch, install mechanical gauge. Test hot: minimum 1.0 bar (15 PSI) at idle, 3.5 bar (50 PSI) at 3000 RPM.

results.label: Low oil pressure (under 1.0 bar hot idle)
results.explanation: Worn oil pump internal gears, clogged oil pickup strainer screen (sludge), or excessive bearing clearances.
results.recommended_action: Drop oil pan, clean pickup tube screen, and replace oil pump.

results.label: Normal oil pressure conforming to manufacturer specs
results.explanation: Hydraulic oil lubrication pressure is healthy.
results.recommended_action: Replace faulty oil pressure sender switch.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect oil pump for wear or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Oil Pump Pressure Relief Valve & Drive Chain
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect pressure relief bypass plunger to verify it is not stuck open by metal debris.

results.label: Worn pump / relief valve stuck open / damaged drive
results.explanation: Relief valve stuck open bleeds pressurized oil straight back to pan without feeding engine galleries.
results.recommended_action: Replace oil pump assembly.

results.label: Pump in good condition with free-moving relief valve
results.explanation: Pump internals are sound.
results.recommended_action: Check crankshaft main and rod bearing wear.

repair_guide.title: Mechanical Oil Pressure Gauge Hookup & Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Ensure engine is switched off when removing pressure switch to prevent hot oil ejection.

steps.title: Remove Oil Pressure Switch
steps.description: Locate 1-pin sensor near oil filter housing, disconnect plug, unscrew sensor with deep socket.

steps.title: Thread Gauge Adapter
steps.description: Screw gauge hose into port, start engine, observe needle. If needle stays near 0, shut engine down in under 5 seconds.

symptoms: Blue smoke from exhaust under acceleration
check_action: Perform dry and wet cylinder compression test across all cylinders (spec: 11-14 bar for petrol, 25-30 bar for diesel).
safety_warning: Worn oil control rings cause oil burning, destroying the catalytic converter and spark plugs.

diagnosis_steps.step: Perform compression test
diagnosis_steps.title: Dry & Wet Cylinder Compression Test
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove all spark plugs, disable fuel pump, screw compression gauge into cylinder 1. Crank engine through 5 compression pulses.

results.label: Low compression on one or more cylinders (below 9 bar)
results.explanation: Worn compression rings, scored cylinder walls, or burned valves allow combustion pressure to leak.
results.recommended_action: Add 1 teaspoon of clean engine oil into cylinder (wet test). If compression jumps up, piston rings are worn.
