results.label: Good compression uniform across all cylinders (within 10%)
results.explanation: Piston rings and valve seating are sealing effectively.
results.recommended_action: If burning oil, inspect valve stem oil seals or turbo seal.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect piston rings for wear or damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check for Excessive Crankcase Blow-By Pressure
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine idling warm, loosen oil filler cap and let it rest on valve cover neck. Check if cap jumps off violently from blow-by pressure.

results.label: Violent blow-by / cap blown off with visible smoke puffing
results.explanation: Combustion gases leaking past worn piston rings pressurize the engine crankcase, pushing oil out through seals.
results.recommended_action: Engine overhaul required: hone cylinders and install new piston rings.

results.label: Slight vacuum or gentle vibration holding cap down
results.explanation: Crankcase pressure is well controlled.
results.recommended_action: Check PCV breather valve.

repair_guide.title: Oil Cap Blow-By "Tea Cup" Test & Compression Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Disable ignition and fuel injection before cranking engine during compression testing.

steps.title: Oil Filler Cap Floating Test
steps.description: Loosen oil cap while engine idles. It should rattle slightly in place; if it shoots off or vents heavy smoke, piston rings are worn.

steps.title: Execute Dry vs Wet Test
steps.description: Record dry readings. Squirt 5ml oil into low cylinder; if reading climbs significantly, piston rings/bores are compromised.

symptoms: Rotten egg / sulfur smell from exhaust
check_action: Measure inlet and outlet temperature using an infrared thermometer (outlet should be 20°C - 50°C hotter than inlet when functioning).
safety_warning: A clogged catalytic converter creates extreme exhaust backpressure, causing severe engine overheating and loss of power.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect catalytic converter for physical damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Tap Converter Body and Check for Broken Ceramic Substrate
diagnosis_steps.description: Hit converter casing with a rubber mallet. Listen for internal loose ceramic honeycomb rattling like stones in a tin can.

results.label: Internal rattle / physical impact dent or cracked welds
results.explanation: Thermal shock or misfire fuel ignition melted and shattered the precious metal ceramic monolith.
results.recommended_action: Replace catalytic converter assembly.

results.label: Converter intact with solid sound
results.explanation: Ceramic core is physically in place.
results.recommended_action: Check catalytic chemical conversion efficiency.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check catalytic converter efficiency
diagnosis_steps.title: Compare Upstream and Downstream O2 Sensor Switching
diagnosis_steps.description: Read live OBD data: upstream O2 sensor should oscillate rapidly between 0.1V and 0.9V, while downstream sensor should stay nearly flat (~0.45V - 0.7V).

results.label: Low efficiency (downstream sensor mirrors upstream switching - P0420)
results.explanation: The catalyst has lost oxygen storage capacity and can no longer reduce CO, NOx, and HC pollutants.
results.recommended_action: Replace catalytic converter and fix upstream engine misfires.

results.label: High efficiency with stable downstream O2 signal
results.explanation: Catalytic oxidation and reduction are functioning properly.
results.recommended_action: Check exhaust pipe joints for air leaks.

repair_guide.title: Infrared Temperature Efficiency Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Exhaust pipes exceed 400°C. Do not touch bare metal.

steps.title: Warm Engine Thoroughly
steps.description: Drive vehicle for 10 minutes to reach full operating temperature.

steps.title: Aim Laser at Inlet and Outlet
steps.description: Measure exhaust pipe right before converter inlet, then right after outlet flange. Outlet MUST be 30°C to 60°C hotter if catalyst is actively burning hydrocarbons.

check_action: Read live O2 sensor voltage (0.1V to 0.9V switching response) and check internal heater circuit resistance.
safety_warning: A failed upstream oxygen sensor forces the ECU into open-loop limp mode, running rich and clogging the catalytic converter.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test oxygen sensor voltage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Upstream O2 Sensor Switching Frequency
diagnosis_steps.description: Observe sensor voltage on OBD live scanner. At hot idle, voltage must cycle cleanly between 0.1V (lean) and 0.9V (rich) every 1 to 2 seconds.

results.label: Low voltage / lazy switching / stuck flatlined signal
results.explanation: Zirconia sensor element is poisoned by silicone, lead, or heavy carbon soot, causing sluggish or dead response.
results.recommended_action: Replace oxygen sensor with direct-fit OEM sensor.

results.label: Normal fast voltage switching (0.1V to 0.9V cycle)
results.explanation: Sensor reads exhaust gas oxygen content accurately.
results.recommended_action: Check sensor internal heater circuit.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect oxygen sensor wiring for damage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Wiring Harness for Melted Insulation & Heater Resistance
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect 4-wire sensor harness where it runs near the hot exhaust manifold. Measure resistance across the two identical heater wires (spec: 4-15 ohms).

results.label: Damaged / melted wiring or open heater circuit
results.explanation: Melted wires ground out or internal heating element burned, preventing sensor from reaching its 350°C operating temperature.
results.recommended_action: Repair heat shielding and replace oxygen sensor.

results.label: Intact wiring harness and good heater resistance
results.explanation: Electrical circuit is in good order.
results.recommended_action: Check for exhaust leaks before the sensor.

repair_guide.title: Oxygen Sensor Replacement & Thread Antisieze
repair_guide.safety_warning: Apply penetrating oil while exhaust is warm (not boiling hot) to break factory thread rust.

steps.title: Unplug Sensor Connector
steps.description: Depress locking clip, disconnect harness before unscrewing so wires do not twist.

steps.title: Unscrew with Slotted 22mm Socket
steps.description: Fit slotted socket over sensor hex, attach breaker bar, and break free.

steps.title: Coat Threads & Torque
steps.description: Ensure new sensor threads have high-temp anti-seize (keep paste off sensor tip!) and torque to 45 Nm.

symptoms: Rough idle / stalling right after refueling at gas station
check_action: Unplug vacuum hose and blow through valve; with no 12V power applied, valve must be closed and airtight.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test canister purge valve operation
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Purge Valve Sealing (Normally Closed)
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove valve from intake manifold. Blow into inlet nipple by mouth or vacuum pump with power disconnected.

results.label: Valve stuck open (air flows freely through valve unpowered)
results.explanation: Solenoid stuck open sucks raw fuel vapor and unmetered air directly into intake manifold, flooding the engine right after refueling.
results.recommended_action: Replace EVAP purge solenoid valve.

results.label: Valve operates correctly (100% airtight when unpowered)
results.explanation: Internal solenoid seat seals airtight.
results.recommended_action: Check purge valve vacuum lines for cracks.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check for leaks in purge valve hoses
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Plastic & Rubber Vapor Lines from Fuel Tank to Engine
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect the thin nylon vapor line routing from the rear fuel tank charcoal canister up to the intake plenum.

results.label: Leaking / split / disconnected vapor hoses
results.explanation: Cracked vapor hose leaks fuel fumes into engine bay and triggers EVAP gross leak code.
results.recommended_action: Replace cracked nylon or rubber EVAP hose section.

results.label: No leaks found in vacuum lines
results.explanation: Lines are sealed.
results.recommended_action: Check charcoal canister under vehicle.

repair_guide.title: EVAP Purge Valve Blow Test & Rapid Replacement
repair_guide.safety_warning: Disconnect electrical connector before removing vacuum hoses.

steps.title: Locate Valve on Intake Plenum
steps.description: Small black plastic cylinder with 2-pin electrical connector and 2 rubber vacuum lines.

steps.title: Unclip and Blow Through
steps.description: Try blowing air through either port. If air passes through easily while disconnected from car, valve is stuck open and defective.

symptoms: Loud ticking or puffing exhaust noise on cold start
Noise quiets down as engine warms up
Visible black soot around cylinder head ports
check_action: Inspect cylinder head exhaust flange with mirror for black soot streaks and check for broken manifold studs.
safety_warning: Exhaust gases contain odorless carbon monoxide (CO) which can enter the cabin through the ventilation system.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect exhaust manifold for cracks or leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Visual Inspection for Hairline Cracks & Carbon Soot Trails
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine cast iron or tubular stainless steel exhaust manifold between cylinder runners for hairline heat cracks.

results.label: Cracked manifold or leaking gasket with visible black soot
results.explanation: Extreme thermal cycling cracks cast iron, producing a sharp rhythmic "tick-tick" noise that mimics valve train lifter tap.
results.recommended_action: Replace cracked exhaust manifold and install multi-layer steel (MLS) gasket.

results.label: Intact manifold without cracks or soot
results.explanation: Manifold body is structurally sound.
results.recommended_action: Check manifold stud bolts torque.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check exhaust manifold bolts for tightness
diagnosis_steps.title: Check for Broken or Snapped Manifold Stud Bolts
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine each cylinder head stud. Often the rearmost or frontmost stud snaps off flush with the cylinder head.

results.label: Loose bolts or broken / missing stud heads
results.explanation: Thermal expansion shears the end studs, lifting the flange and allowing exhaust gas to blast past the gasket.
results.recommended_action: Extract broken studs and install new high-tensile stainless exhaust studs and copper locknuts.

results.label: All bolts tight and torqued to spec
results.explanation: Manifold flange is clamped evenly.
results.recommended_action: Inspect downpipe flex pipe.

repair_guide.title: Cold-Start Exhaust Leak Smoke / Bubble Tracing
repair_guide.safety_warning: Only spray soapy water when engine is COMPLETELY COLD. Do not spray on hot exhaust manifolds.

steps.title: Cold Engine Spray
steps.description: Spray soapy water along manifold gasket seam before starting engine.

steps.title: Start Engine & Watch for Bubbles
steps.description: Start cold engine. Escaping exhaust gas will instantly blow large soap foam bubbles at the leak site within 10 seconds.

check_action: Read live MAP voltage with ignition ON engine OFF (should read ~4.8V / 100 kPa ambient) and check vacuum hose.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test M.A.P. sensor voltage
diagnosis_steps.title: Check MAP Sensor Reference & Output Voltage
diagnosis_steps.description: Measure 5V reference wire, ground wire, and signal wire with multimeter or OBD scanner. Output should drop from ~4.5V down to ~1.2V at idle vacuum.

results.label: Voltage stuck / low voltage / out of range
results.explanation: Internal silicon diaphragm contaminated with oil sludge or piezoresistive circuit failed.
results.recommended_action: Clean sensor snout with electronic cleaner or replace MAP sensor.

results.label: Normal voltage responding instantly to throttle blips
results.explanation: MAP sensor electronic response is normal.
results.recommended_action: Inspect vacuum hose and O-ring seal.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect M.A.P. sensor vacuum hose / O-ring
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Vacuum Hose or Mounting O-Ring for Air Leaks
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect small rubber vacuum hose or green rubber seal ring where sensor mounts into plastic intake manifold.

results.label: Leaking / cracked hose or flattened O-ring
results.explanation: Vacuum leak causes false high pressure reading, tricking ECU into injecting far too much fuel.
results.recommended_action: Replace rubber vacuum hose or sensor O-ring.

results.label: Intact hose with airtight seal
results.explanation: Vacuum connection is airtight.
results.recommended_action: Check throttle body and throttle position sensor.

repair_guide.title: MAP Sensor Cleaning & O-Ring Service
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not insert screwdrivers or sharp objects into sensor port hole; diaphragm will rupture.

steps.title: Remove Single Screw
steps.description: Unplug 3-pin connector, remove single retaining screw on intake manifold.

steps.title: Spray Sensor Port
steps.description: Spray electrical cleaner into hole to dissolve oil blow-by gunk. Allow to dry 5 minutes before reinstalling.

symptoms: Dashboard lights dim when key turned
check_action: Test resting battery voltage with multimeter (12.6V = 100%, 12.0V = discharged) and check for white/blue terminal corrosion.
safety_warning: Car batteries produce explosive hydrogen gas during charging. Keep sparks and open flames away.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test battery voltage
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Resting & Cranking Battery Voltage
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine off, touch multimeter leads to battery posts: 12.6V is fully charged. Have a helper crank engine: voltage must not drop below 9.6V.

results.label: Low voltage (resting < 12.2V or cranking drops below 9.0V)
results.explanation: Sulfated lead plates or bad cells cannot provide the 300A-500A required by the starter motor.
results.recommended_action: Charge battery overnight with smart charger. If it fails load test, replace 12V battery.

results.label: Sufficient voltage (12.6V resting, holds > 10.0V cranking)
results.explanation: Battery charge state and internal resistance are healthy.
results.recommended_action: Inspect battery terminal clamps and starter motor.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect battery terminals for corrosion
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Lead Posts for White/Blue Powdery Corrosion & Tightness
diagnosis_steps.description: Grab battery cable clamps and try to twist them by hand. They should be rock solid and free of corrosion.

results.label: Corroded / loose terminals
results.explanation: Lead sulfate powder creates high contact resistance, cutting starter motor current and clicking starter solenoid.
results.recommended_action: Scrub terminals with baking soda water and wire brush, then coat with dielectric grease.

results.label: Clean, tight terminals with bare metal contact
results.explanation: Electrical connection to battery posts is clean.
results.recommended_action: Inspect starter motor and engine ground strap.

repair_guide.title: Battery Terminal Cleaning & Voltage State Test
tools_needed: Baking soda dissolved in warm water
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always disconnect NEGATIVE (-) terminal first, and reconnect negative LAST to prevent short circuits with wrench.

steps.title: Disconnect Negative Then Positive
steps.description: Loosen 10mm bolt on black negative cable clamp, lift off, then disconnect positive red cable.

steps.title: Neutralize Acid Crust
steps.description: Pour baking soda solution over terminals; it will fizz as it neutralizes battery acid. Scrub with wire brush until shiny metal.

steps.title: Reinstall & Protect
steps.description: Reconnect positive then negative, tighten firmly, and smear grease over clamp to prevent future oxidation.

symptoms: Battery warning light on while driving
Battery goes flat overnight or while driving
check_action: Measure voltage across battery terminals while engine idles with headlights and heater blower turned ON (should read 13.8V to 14.5V).
safety_warning: If alternator fails while driving, the vehicle will stall as soon as the battery drains, losing power steering and brake assist.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test alternator output
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Regulated Alternator Charging Voltage Under Load
diagnosis_steps.description: Start engine, turn on high beams and rear defroster. Measure voltage across battery terminals with digital multimeter.

results.label: Low output (below 13.5V engine running) or overcharging (> 15.2V)
results.explanation: Worn alternator carbon brushes, blown diode rectifier bridge, or failed internal voltage regulator.
results.recommended_action: Replace alternator or voltage regulator/brush pack.

results.label: Normal output (solid 13.8V to 14.4V)
results.explanation: Alternator is charging battery and carrying electrical load.
results.recommended_action: Check serpentine drive belt tension.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check alternator belt tension
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Serpentine Belt Slippage on Alternator Pulley
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect belt tensioner and check if alternator pulley spins freely without squealing under high electrical load.

results.label: Loose / slipping belt
results.explanation: Slipping belt cannot spin alternator fast enough to produce required amperage under load.
results.recommended_action: Tighten manual tensioner or replace weak automatic spring tensioner.

results.label: Properly tensioned belt with no slip
results.explanation: Belt drive is transferring full mechanical power.
results.recommended_action: Inspect battery condition and main B+ cable.

repair_guide.title: Alternator Charging Voltage Quick Meter Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Keep multimeter probe leads away from spinning engine fan blades and drive belts.

steps.title: Baseline Resting Check
steps.description: Measure battery with engine off (approx 12.5V).

steps.title: Start Engine & Read Jump
steps.description: Start engine. Voltage should immediately leap to between 13.8V and 14.5V. If it remains at 12.5V, alternator is not charging.

symptoms: Single loud click when key is turned
Starter spins freely with whining sound without turning engine
check_action: Check for 12V signal on small ignition wire at starter solenoid while turning key to START.
safety_warning: Ensure vehicle is in Neutral (or Park) with handbrake set before testing starter motor terminals.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test starter motor solenoid
diagnosis_steps.title: Check 12V Trigger Signal at Solenoid Terminal 50
diagnosis_steps.description: Attach test light or multimeter probe to small trigger wire on starter. Turn ignition key to START position.

results.label: Faulty solenoid (12V trigger present but starter clicks or does nothing)
results.explanation: Burned copper contact disc inside solenoid prevents main battery current from reaching starter motor windings.
results.recommended_action: Tap starter body with hammer; if it starts, replace starter motor assembly.

results.label: Solenoid working properly and engaging
results.explanation: Electrical solenoid engagement is functional.
results.recommended_action: Check starter motor brushes and flywheel ring gear teeth.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect starter motor brushes for wear
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Starter Internal Carbon Brushes & Bendix Drive
diagnosis_steps.description: Check if starter motor whines without spinning the engine (bendix one-way clutch slipping) or draws zero current (worn brushes).

results.label: Worn brushes or slipping bendix drive gear
results.explanation: Worn carbon brushes no longer make contact with commutator, creating an open circuit dead spot.
results.recommended_action: Replace starter motor assembly.

results.label: Brushes in good condition and bendix teeth intact
results.explanation: Starter internal mechanics are sound.
results.recommended_action: Check battery cables and ignition switch.

repair_guide.title: Starter "Tap" Test & Trigger Wire Voltage Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Disconnect battery ground before unbolting starter heavy 12V positive cable.

steps.title: The Starter Tap Technique
steps.description: If car clicks and won’t crank, have a helper hold key in START position while you firmly tap the starter motor housing with a wooden handle. If it cranks, starter brushes are worn.

steps.title: Test Light on Terminal 50
steps.description: Probe small trigger wire. If test light illuminates in START, ignition switch, relay, and clutch interlock switch are working.

symptoms: Difficulty starting engine in wet weather
check_action: Mist ignition wires with a water spray bottle in darkness while engine idles; look for blue sparks jumping to ground.
safety_warning: Secondary ignition voltage reaches 25,000 to 45,000 volts. Do not touch bare wires while engine runs.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect distributor cap / ignition coils for cracks or carbon tracks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Distributor Cap / Coil-on-Plug Boots for Carbon Tracking
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine inside of distributor cap or rubber spark plug coil boots for faint grey carbon lightning tracks or hairline cracks.

results.label: Cracked / damaged cap / carbon tracks on coil boots
results.explanation: High voltage spark flashes over carbon tracks directly to engine block rather than firing inside spark plug gap.
results.recommended_action: Replace distributor cap and rotor, or replace damaged ignition coil boots.

results.label: Cap & boots in good condition without tracking
results.explanation: Insulation is clean and intact.
results.recommended_action: Check ignition spark plug wire continuity.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test ignition wires for continuity & spark plug boots
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Ignition Wire Resistance with Multimeter
diagnosis_steps.description: Measure resistance end-to-end on each spark plug wire (standard rule: approx 3,000 to 7,000 ohms per foot).

results.label: Broken wire / resistance over 25kΩ or punctured boot
results.explanation: Internal carbon conductive core broken, creating high resistance and weak spark that blows out under compression.
results.recommended_action: Install a new set of high-temperature silicone spark plug ignition wires.

results.label: Wires intact with uniform resistance
results.explanation: High voltage wire continuity is healthy.
results.recommended_action: Check spark plugs gap and condition.

repair_guide.title: Water Mist Dark Test & Spark Plug Wire Replacement
repair_guide.safety_warning: Change spark plug wires ONE AT A TIME to preserve firing order (e.g., 1-3-4-2).

steps.title: Night Water Mist Test
steps.description: In a dark garage or at night, mist water gently over spark plug wires while engine idles. Blue electrical arcing reveals cracked insulation.

steps.title: Apply Dielectric Silicone
steps.description: Smear a pea-sized amount of dielectric silicone grease inside new boots to seal out water and prevent boot sticking.

symptoms: Grinding or crunching sound inside door
check_action: Listen at door panel while pressing switch for motor hum, and test power at motor connector.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test power to window motor
diagnosis_steps.title: Test 12V Power & Ground Reversal at Motor Plug
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove door panel trim, unplug 2-pin motor connector, attach test light, and press window switch UP and DOWN.

results.label: No power to window motor
results.explanation: Broken wires in flexible door jamb rubber boot accordion, blown window fuse, or faulty master window switch.
results.recommended_action: Repair severed door hinge harness wires or replace window switch.

results.label: Power and ground present when switch pressed
results.explanation: Switch and wiring deliver full battery voltage.
results.recommended_action: Check motor windings and regulator cables.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect window regulator mechanism
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Regulator Cable Spool and Plastic Glass Clips
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine steel cables inside door. Check if cable is tangled in drive spool or plastic guide slider clip is broken.

results.label: Damaged regulator / snapped cable / broken plastic clips
results.explanation: Steel cable frayed and jammed around motor spool, causing glass to drop down into door or freeze stuck.
results.recommended_action: Replace window regulator assembly (mechanism + motor).

results.label: Mechanism functioning freely and intact
results.explanation: Cables and tracks are aligned.
results.recommended_action: Clean window rubber channel felt and lubricate with silicone spray.

repair_guide.title: Door Card Removal & Window Regulator Replacement
repair_guide.safety_warning: Tape window glass securely to top door frame with masking tape before unbolting regulator.

steps.title: Secure Window Glass
steps.description: Pull glass up by hand and tape securely across door frame with heavy painter tape.

steps.title: Remove Door Panel Card
steps.description: Remove hidden screws behind armrest and door pull, pop perimeter plastic clips with trim tool, unhook cable.

steps.title: Unbolt Regulator & Swap
steps.description: Unbolt glass clamps, unbolt motor and regulator rails, slide out through door access opening and replace.

symptoms: Headlight not working on one side
check_action: Inspect bulb halogen filament for breakage and check plastic socket connector for heat melting.
safety_warning: Do NOT touch new halogen or xenon bulb glass with bare fingers; skin oils create hot spots and shatter the glass.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect headlamp bulb for filament condition
diagnosis_steps.title: Remove Bulb and Check Tungsten Filament Under Light
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove rubber dust cap, unclip spring wire, pull out H7/H4 bulb. Look for broken wire filament or dark silver deposit inside bulb glass.

results.label: Burnt out / broken filament or black bulb glass
results.explanation: Filament reached end of lifespan (approx 500-800 hours for standard halogens).
results.recommended_action: Install a new high-quality headlight bulb. Replace both sides for matching light output.

results.label: Filament intact and continuous
results.explanation: Bulb filament is complete.
results.recommended_action: Check socket connector and headlight fuse.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check headlamp socket for corrosion or melting
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Plastic Plug and Female Spade Terminals
diagnosis_steps.description: Look inside plastic socket for melted brown plastic, green corrosion, or loose loose spade grips.

results.label: Corroded / melted socket connector
results.explanation: High electrical resistance generates extreme heat at connector pins, melting socket and causing intermittent lighting.
results.recommended_action: Splice in a ceramic replacement headlight bulb pigtail connector.

results.label: Clean socket with tight terminal tension
results.explanation: Socket contact is sound.
results.recommended_action: Check dedicated left/right headlight fuse in underhood box.

repair_guide.title: Headlight Bulb Replacement Without Touching Glass
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always handle bulbs by their metal base only. If glass is touched, wipe clean with isopropyl alcohol.

steps.title: Remove Waterproof Dust Cap
steps.description: Behind headlamp assembly, twist or peel back round rubber dust cover.

steps.title: Unclip Spring Retainer
steps.description: Press wire spring clip inward and toward side to unhook from stamped metal notch.

steps.title: Align Index Tab
steps.description: Insert new bulb aligning alignment tab into notch, re-hook wire spring, re-seat rubber cap tightly.

symptoms: Wipers operate intermittently or stop mid-windshield
Motor whines but blades don't sweep
check_action: Check wiper fuse, listen for motor hum under cowl, and check if linkage ball joints have popped off.
safety_warning: Driving in heavy rain with failed wipers creates immediate zero-visibility hazard.

diagnosis_steps.step: Test power to wiper motor
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Voltage at Wiper Motor Connector
diagnosis_steps.description: Switch wipers to LOW and HIGH. Probe wiper motor harness pins with test light or multimeter.

results.label: No power to wiper motor
results.explanation: Blown 25A/30A wiper fuse (often blown when wipers frozen to glass in winter), bad relay, or steering column stalk switch failure.
results.recommended_action: Replace wiper fuse and test stalk switch.

results.label: Power present at motor connector on all speed settings
results.explanation: Electrical feed is operational.
results.recommended_action: Check mechanical linkage rods and motor internal park switch.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect wiper motor linkage for wear
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Transmission Linkage Ball Joints & Pivot Bushings
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove plastic cowl cover and inspect metal wiper transmission arms. Check if plastic ball socket joint has popped apart.

results.label: Worn / popped off linkage ball joint or seized pivot shafts
results.explanation: Road grime seizes the pivot shafts or plastic ball socket wears out, detaching the arms from the motor crank.
results.recommended_action: Replace wiper transmission linkage assembly and lubricate pivots.

results.label: Intact linkage connected securely to motor arm
results.explanation: Mechanical rods are firmly coupled.
results.recommended_action: Inspect wiper motor internal brush gear.

repair_guide.title: Wiper Linkage Emergency Reattachment & Motor Swap
repair_guide.safety_warning: Mark wiper blade resting positions on glass with masking tape before unbolting wiper arms.

steps.title: Mark Blade Alignment
steps.description: Place strip of tape along blade edge on windshield to reinstall at identical angle.

steps.title: Remove Wiper Arms & Cowl
steps.description: Pry off nut caps, remove 13mm nuts, use small puller to pop arm off tapered splined shaft, remove plastic cowl clips.

steps.title: Replace Linkage Assembly
steps.description: Unbolt 3 motor/linkage bolts, disconnect harness, fit new assembly, and park motor before tightening arms.

symptoms: Clutch pedal feels spongy or stays on floor
Fluid leak near clutch pedal inside car
check_action: Check brake/clutch shared fluid reservoir level and inspect carpet above clutch pedal for damp oily residue.
safety_warning: Loss of clutch hydraulic pressure leaves vehicle permanently in gear or unable to shift.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check clutch master cylinder for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Clutch Master Cylinder Pushrod Above Footwell Pedal
diagnosis_steps.description: Look up under driver dashboard where clutch pedal pushrod enters the firewall master cylinder boot for fluid leaks.

results.label: Leaking cylinder (wet brake fluid on pedal arm / carpet)
results.explanation: Internal piston seal worn, letting fluid leak into cabin and introducing air bubbles into hydraulic line.
results.recommended_action: Replace clutch master cylinder and bleed hydraulic system.

results.label: Dry pushrod and intact cylinder casing
results.explanation: Master cylinder shows no signs of external leakage.
results.recommended_action: Inspect slave cylinder on transmission bellhousing.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check clutch slave cylinder for leaks & fluid level
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Clutch Slave Cylinder on Transmission Bellhousing
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect external slave cylinder rubber dust boot on gearbox (or concentric slave cylinder bellhousing weep hole).

results.label: Leaking slave cylinder or low fluid level
results.explanation: Slave cylinder piston seal failure loses pressure to throwout bearing, preventing clutch disengagement.
results.recommended_action: Replace clutch slave cylinder and pressure bleed line.

results.label: No leaks detected and fluid level is full
results.explanation: Hydraulic cylinders are holding pressure.
results.recommended_action: If clutch slips or chatters, friction plate is worn out.

repair_guide.title: Clutch Hydraulic Bleeding & Cylinder Inspection
repair_guide.safety_warning: Clutch systems share fluid with brake reservoir on many cars; never let fluid drop below feed nipple.

steps.title: Fill Reservoir to Maximum
steps.description: Keep fluid filled to brim while bleeding to avoid drawing air into clutch pickup port.

steps.title: Pump and Hold
steps.description: Have helper pump pedal 5 times, hold to floor. Open slave cylinder bleed screw 1 turn, let air and fluid rush out, close screw.

steps.title: Repeat Until Solid Resistance
steps.description: Repeat 4 to 5 cycles until no air bubbles appear and pedal returns with firm snap.

symptoms: Transmission slipping (engine revs but car doesn't accelerate)
Delay in gear engagement into Drive/Reverse
check_action: Check ATF fluid level and color on dipstick (or overflow plug at 40°C): should be clear red, not black or smelling burned.
safety_warning: Driving with low ATF level burns internal clutch friction plates and overheats the torque converter.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check transmission fluid level and condition
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Automatic Transmission Fluid (ATF) Level & Color
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine idling warm in Park, pull ATF dipstick (or check level plug at 35°C-45°C). Wipe on white paper towel: check if dark brown/black with burnt smell.

results.label: Low / dirty / burned black fluid
results.explanation: Low fluid level starves hydraulic pump, causing clutch slip and delayed gear engagements.
results.recommended_action: Perform complete ATF drain and refill with manufacturer spec fluid and replace filter.

results.label: Clean, translucent red / amber fluid at correct level
results.explanation: Fluid level and hydraulic properties are adequate.
results.recommended_action: Inspect transmission solenoids and pan seals.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect transmission filter and pan for leaks or metal debris
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Transmission Pan Gasket & Magnet Sediment
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect pan perimeter for wet fluid leaks. Drop pan to inspect internal filter and magnet for metallic silver flake buildup.

results.label: Clogged filter / heavy metal shavings on magnet / pan leak
results.explanation: Clogged suction filter restricts oil flow to valve body; metal flakes indicate mechanical clutch or planetary wear.
results.recommended_action: Clean pan, replace internal filter and pan gasket, and refill fresh fluid.

results.label: Clean filter and dry transmission pan
results.explanation: No abnormal metal debris or pan leaks found.
results.recommended_action: Perform electronic diagnostic scan for shift solenoid codes.

repair_guide.title: Automatic Transmission Fluid Level Check & Pan Service
tools_needed: OBD scanner to monitor ATF temp
repair_guide.safety_warning: Vehicle must be level on lift/jack stands and transmission fluid temperature strictly between 35°C and 45°C when checking overflow plug.

steps.title: Warm Up Transmission
steps.description: Drive vehicle or idle until ATF temperature reads 40°C on diagnostic tool.

steps.title: Shift Through All Gears
steps.description: Foot on brake, shift P -> R -> N -> D -> 1 holding 3 seconds in each position, return to Park.

steps.title: Verify Steady Stream
steps.description: Remove overflow level plug with engine idling. Fluid should drip out as a thin pencil stream. If nothing drips, add fluid.

symptoms: Driveline vibration through floorboard at 80-110 km/h
Clunking noise when shifting from Drive to Reverse
Clicking noise when turning sharp corners
check_action: Grab driveshaft / CV axle by hand and twist firmly to check for rotational free play in U-joint caps or torn rubber boots.
safety_warning: A severed driveshaft universal joint at highway speed can drop and vault the vehicle.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect universal joint / CV joint for wear or play
diagnosis_steps.title: Check U-Joint Cross Bearing Play & CV Rubber Boot Integrity
diagnosis_steps.description: Inspect cross trunnions for rusty needle bearing dust and twist driveshaft in opposite directions across joint.

results.label: Worn / sloppy play detected or torn rubber boot slinging grease
results.explanation: Needle bearings crushed from lack of grease, producing severe driveline vibration and clunking.
results.recommended_action: Replace universal joint cross bearing or complete CV half-shaft axle assembly.

results.label: Joint in good condition with zero radial play
results.explanation: Universal joints and CV joints are tight.
results.recommended_action: Check driveshaft center support bearing and driveline balance.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check driveline alignment and center bearing
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect Center Support Carrier Bearing Rubber & Shaft Balance
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine center rubber doughnut carrier bearing for tears and check for missing welded balance weights on steel tube.

results.label: Torn center support bearing or missing balance weight
results.explanation: Driveshaft whips under rotational speed, transmitting high-frequency vibration through vehicle floor.
results.recommended_action: Replace center support bearing and rebalance driveshaft.

results.label: Properly aligned and balanced driveline
results.explanation: Driveline balance and support are correct.
results.recommended_action: Check differential pinion bearing.

repair_guide.title: U-Joint Play Inspection & CV Boot Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Transmission must be in Neutral to relieve drivetrain binding before checking driveshaft rotation by hand.

steps.title: Chock Wheels and Set Neutral
steps.description: Safely block tires with chocks, shift transmission into Neutral so driveshaft can turn freely.

steps.title: Twist Cross Joint
steps.description: Firmly grasp each side of the universal joint and twist in opposite directions. Any visual movement between cross and yoke means bearing failure.

symptoms: Whining noise from rear end under acceleration
check_action: Check differential gear oil level and inspect magnetic drain plug for metal shards or low fluid.
safety_warning: A differential running dry of gear oil will seize the drive wheels at speed.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect differential fluid level and condition
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Gear Oil Level & Inspect for Metallic Shimmer
diagnosis_steps.description: Remove fill plug on differential housing. Fluid level should be level with bottom of fill hole. Check for burnt smell or glitter.

results.label: Low / dirty / metallic silver gear oil
results.explanation: Oil starvation or breakdown causes ring and pinion bevel gear teeth to gall and whine under acceleration.
results.recommended_action: Drain fluid, inspect gears, and refill with specified heavy gear oil (e.g., 75W-90 GL-5 / LS).

results.label: Clean and sufficient fluid level
results.explanation: Lubrication level is correct.
results.recommended_action: Inspect pinion and carrier bearings for wear.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check for differential bearing wear & gear backlash
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Pinion Bearing Play and Gear Mesh Backlash
diagnosis_steps.description: Wiggle differential pinion input flange up and down by hand to test tapered roller bearing play.

results.label: Worn bearings / excessive radial play or pitted gear teeth
results.explanation: Pinion bearings worn out, changing gear contact pattern and generating distinctive howling whine.
results.recommended_action: Rebuild differential with new bearings and crush sleeve, and reset ring-and-pinion backlash.

results.label: Bearings in good condition with tight tolerances
results.explanation: Differential bearings are tight.
results.recommended_action: Check wheel bearings on rear axle.

repair_guide.title: Differential Fluid Inspection & Pinion Seal Check
repair_guide.safety_warning: Differential fluid has a strong sulfur odor; wear nitrile gloves.

steps.title: ALWAYS Remove FILL Plug First
steps.description: Never drain differential until you confirm the upper fill plug unscrews cleanly.

steps.title: Inspect Magnet Plug
steps.description: Wipe drain plug magnet. Fine gray paste is normal wear; large metal flakes or gear tooth chips indicate mechanical failure.

symptoms: Whining / groaning noise when turning steering wheel
Fluid leak under front of engine
check_action: Check power steering reservoir fluid dipstick level and check for bubbles / foaming while engine runs.
safety_warning: Sudden loss of power steering assist while parking or cornering dramatically increases steering effort.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect power steering fluid level
diagnosis_steps.title: Check Fluid Level on Reservoir Dipstick
diagnosis_steps.description: Engine idling, turn steering wheel lock-to-lock twice. Check reservoir level against COLD / HOT marks. Check if fluid is brown or aerated.

results.label: Low fluid level / aerated frothy foam
results.explanation: Low fluid draws air into pump vanes (cavitation), creating loud whining noise and steering stiffness.
results.recommended_action: Top up with correct ATF / CHF power steering fluid, bleed air, and trace leaks.

results.label: Sufficient clean fluid level without air bubbles
results.explanation: Hydraulic fluid level is optimal.
results.recommended_action: Inspect pump shaft bearing and pressure hoses.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check power steering pump and hoses for leaks
diagnosis_steps.title: Inspect High-Pressure Steering Hoses and Steering Rack Boots
diagnosis_steps.description: Examine high-pressure crimped steering hose connections and rubber steering rack tie-rod boots for wet oil seepage.

results.label: Leaking pump / crimp hose / rack seal leak
results.explanation: Cracked high pressure line or leaking steering rack end seals vent hydraulic pressure.
results.recommended_action: Replace leaking power steering pressure line or steering rack assembly.

results.label: Pump and hoses in good dry condition
results.explanation: System is sealed and leak-free.
results.recommended_action: Inspect serpentine belt and tensioner.

repair_guide.title: Power Steering Air Bleeding & Level Adjustment
repair_guide.safety_warning: Do not hold steering wheel at full lock against stops for more than 5 seconds; this overheats pump relief valve.

steps.title: Raise Front Wheels Off Ground
steps.description: Lift front axle on jack stands so tires turn freely without ground friction.

steps.title: Lock-to-Lock Bleed Engine Off
steps.description: With engine OFF and reservoir cap open, turn wheel slowly lock-to-lock 15 times to purge trapped air bubbles into reservoir.

steps.title: Top Up Fluid Level
steps.description: Verify fluid is bubble-free, top up to FULL mark, start engine and verify silence.

symptoms: Grinding / roaring humming noise that gets louder with speed
Noise changes tone when swerving left and right
Wheel wobbling / play when rocked by hand
check_action: Jack up wheel and grasp tire at 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions, rock firmly back and forth to detect bearing play.
safety_warning: A completely failed wheel bearing can seize solid or allow the wheel and hub to detach from vehicle at highway speeds.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check wheel bearing for play
diagnosis_steps.title: Rock Tire at 12 and 6 O'clock Positions
diagnosis_steps.description: Raise corner on jack stand. Place one hand at 12 o'clock and other at 6 o'clock on tire tread; push and pull firmly.

results.label: Loose / clunking / worn bearing with noticeable play
results.explanation: Internal steel ball/roller bearings and races are pitted and worn, creating dangerous free play.
results.recommended_action: Replace wheel bearing / hub assembly unit.

results.label: Bearing in good condition with zero free play
results.explanation: Bearing assembly is tight.
results.recommended_action: Spin wheel to listen for internal roughness.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect bearing for signs of damage, rough spinning, or corrosion
diagnosis_steps.title: Spin Wheel by Hand and Feel Suspension Spring for Vibration
diagnosis_steps.description: Spin raised tire rapidly by hand while holding coil spring with fingers. If spring vibrates like a coarse guitar string, bearing is pitted.

results.label: Rough growling spin / vibration felt through suspension spring
results.explanation: Spalling of bearing race creates roaring vibration transferred through knuckle and strut.
results.recommended_action: Install new wheel bearing and torque axle nut to factory specification.

results.label: Smooth, silent spin without vibration
results.explanation: Bearing rolls silently.
results.recommended_action: Check tire for cupping or tread feathering.

repair_guide.title: Wheel Bearing Coil Spring Vibration Test
repair_guide.safety_warning: Never crawl under vehicle supported only by a jack. Always support firmly on jack stand.

steps.title: Raise Suspect Wheel
steps.description: Lift vehicle corner off ground so tire spins freely.

steps.title: The Spring Stethoscope Test
steps.description: Place hand firmly on the metal coil spring. Spin the tire fast with your other hand. A healthy bearing feels silky smooth; a bad bearing transmits intense buzzing vibration directly into your fingers.

symptoms: Low tire pressure symbol flashing for 60s then solid
check_action: Check cold tire pressure on all 4 tires (and spare) with gauge against door jamb sticker spec (e.g., 2.3 bar / 33 PSI).
safety_warning: Underinflated tires generate extreme internal friction heat, causing tire tread delamination and blowouts.

diagnosis_steps.step: Check tire pressures with gauge
diagnosis_steps.title: Measure Cold Pressure on All 4 Tires with Calibrated Gauge
diagnosis_steps.description: Read pressure on each tire when cold. Compare against recommended PSI values listed on driver B-pillar door placard.

results.label: Low / incorrect tire pressure detected (below threshold)
results.explanation: Puncture, slow nail leak, or seasonal cold weather dropped pressure below 25% safety threshold.
results.recommended_action: Inflate tire to specified pressure on door sticker and reset TPMS system.

results.label: All tire pressures correct and matched
results.explanation: Tire inflation pressures match factory specifications.
results.recommended_action: Inspect TPMS valve stem sensors.

diagnosis_steps.step: Inspect TPMS sensors for damage, corrosion, or dead battery
diagnosis_steps.title: Check TPMS Sensor Radio Transmission & Battery Life
diagnosis_steps.description: Scan sensor with TPMS diagnostic tool to read internal battery state (batteries typically last 7 to 10 years).

results.label: Dead sensor battery / damaged / corroded valve stem
results.explanation: Internal lithium coin cell dead or aluminum valve stem cracked from road salt corrosion.
results.recommended_action: Replace TPMS sensor and calibrate sensor ID to vehicle ECU.

results.label: Clean, intact sensors transmitting strong RF signal
results.explanation: TPMS sensors are broadcasting pressure and temperature data.
results.recommended_action: Perform TPMS reset calibration in instrument cluster.

repair_guide.title: Tire Pressure Reset & Door Placard Verification
repair_guide.safety_warning: Always check pressures when tires have been parked for at least 3 hours; driving heats air and raises pressure artificially.

steps.title: Read Driver Door Pillar Sticker
steps.description: Open driver door, look at white/yellow placard for exact FRONT and REAR pressure specs in bar or PSI.

steps.title: Adjust All 4 Tires
steps.description: Inflate or deflate each tire precisely to placard spec.

steps.title: Initiate TPMS Reset
steps.description: In vehicle infotainment or dashboard menu, select "Vehicle Settings" -> "Tyre Pressure" -> "SET" and drive for 10 minutes to learn.
